docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Briefing (trap): Sur-replies are discouraged and need leave by motion; any sur-reply should be concise. No letter briefs for requests for relief; file everything on CM/ECF. But new controlling case law decided after briefing closes should be brought to the judge’s attention by a short letter brief, to which the other side may respond. Follow Local Rule 7(b) strictly on extensions and state good cause. Reconsideration motions should be timely, sparing, and only with a persuasive reason that might change the court’s mind.

docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Chambers copies: Courtesy copies of e-filed papers are not generally required, but chambers copies of particularly lengthy motions with exhibits are greatly appreciated.

docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Settlement conferences (trap): A pre-settlement telephone conference usually sets the date and what must be exchanged or done beforehand. Ex parte memoranda are due 7 days before the conference, and parties must exchange offers and counter-offers in advance; a party claiming damages must give opposing counsel a damages analysis. Clients must attend unless previously excused; an entity must send a representative fully authorized to decide all matters in the case. Scheduling a settlement conference does not change existing deadlines unless a separate order for good cause says so. If the case doesn’t settle, the judge encourages continued talks and contact by letter or email. In cases assigned to Judge Richardson, another magistrate judge may be asked to handle the settlement conference.

docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Rule 26(f) reports
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Rule 26(f) reports: Give serious consideration to Rule 26(f). The judge usually defers to agreed schedules unless the case is mismanaged but urges realistic deadlines, and resolves scheduling disputes by telephone conference.

docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Social Security cases: deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Social Security cases: deadlines (trap): The standing scheduling order controls over any prior order and over CM/ECF auto-deadlines. The Commissioner answers and files the record within 60 days after service on the agency, Attorney General, and U.S. Attorney; plaintiff’s motion to reverse is due 60 days after the answer; defendant’s motion to affirm, treated as the response, is due 60 days later; plaintiff may reply within 14 days. If neither party acts within 7 months of the complaint, a Local Rule 41(a) notice issues. EAJA fee motions are due within 30 days after judgment becomes final and must attest that the movant first tried to settle fees with opposing counsel. Extensions are discouraged and should generally be 30 days at most, with good cause under Local Rule 7(b)(2).

docs.t: Judge Robert A. Richardson (D. Conn.) — Social Security cases: briefs
docs.x: Judge Robert A. Richardson, D. Conn.. Social Security cases: briefs: Briefs are capped at 40 pages, but the court would appreciate 25 pages where the record is not voluminous and no novel issues are raised. Double-space the body (block quotes and footnotes may be single), one-inch margins, and consecutive page numbers; footnotes and block quotes may not be used to evade limits. Skip boilerplate on the standard of review and the sequential evaluation process and focus on applying controlling law to the disputed facts. Citing unreported district court decisions is discouraged; if cited, attach them as exhibits.

docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. Discovery disputes (trap): In referred cases, Judge Spector follows any procedure the referring District Judge set. In all-purpose cases (or referrals with no set procedure), raise disputes by a written motion that complies with Local Rule 37 or by a joint status report detailing the dispute. The judge accepts CM/ECF letters summarizing disputes and tries informal resolution, but generally prefers on-the-record video conferences, sometimes with a briefing schedule set in advance. Disputes are occasionally ruled on from the bench. No telephone calls about discovery disputes except in emergencies (e.g., a deposition impasse with out-of-state deponents), and then only with counsel for all parties on the line.

docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. Oral argument: Argument is at the judge’s discretion, with no set days; the court tries to accommodate counsel’s schedules. To ask for argument, include a request in a letter accompanying the motion. Less experienced lawyers familiar with the matter are encouraged to argue, and the judge will hear from more than one attorney per party.

docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Motion practice
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. Motion practice: All requests for relief should be made by motion on CM/ECF and/or orally on the record, not by letter. Sur-replies are discouraged and require leave on motion; if allowed, keep them concise. New controlling case law decided after briefing closes should be flagged in a short letter brief on the docket so the other side can respond. Reconsideration motions: timely and sparing, only for a persuasive reason or overlooked precedent; they must cite the reconsideration standard and concisely state the basis.

docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Extensions of time (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Scheduling and Rule 26(f) reports
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. Scheduling and Rule 26(f) reports: A reasonable, efficient 26(f) report typically becomes the initial scheduling order. Scheduling disputes are usually resolved by telephonic conference with counsel.

docs.t: Judge Robert M. Spector (D. Conn.) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert M. Spector, D. Conn.. Settlement conferences (trap): A pre-settlement telephonic conference sets the date, information exchanges, and open issues; a detailed order follows. docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. docs.x: Judge Joy Flowers Conti, W.D. Pa.. Correspondence, chambers, and courtesy copies: Correspondence is disfavored except to report status (e.g., mediation); to get action, file a motion. Requested copies of voluminous filings must be ECF-stamped printouts, 3-hole punched in black binders no thicker than 3 inches, labeled on cover and spine. Participants’ pronoun or title preferences may be sent by email to tyler_klein@pawd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and settlement
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and settlement: Joint pre-conference statement (3 pages maximum: facts, claims and defenses, discovery status, trial cost and time estimate, relief sought) due at least 5 business days before the initial case management and post-discovery conferences, and before settlement conferences. Each party may add an optional voluntary position statement of up to 8 pages. The initial conference is usually within 30 days of all answers and is presumptively by phone; lead trial counsel must participate. Settlement conferences, final pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are not ordinarily by phone. Settlement conferences (mainly for jury cases): lead trial counsel and client representatives with full authority attend in person; insurer representatives with full authority up to policy limits attend in person or by phone. No one leaves until excused.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions, sealing, and TROs
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Extensions, sealing, and TROs: Extension requests: a short motion with supporting facts, opposing counsel’s position, and a proposed scheduling order adjusting affected dates, filed at least 5 business days before the deadline. Opponents of short extensions must show actual prejudice. Motions to seal must state the specific factual and legal basis, and the proposed order must include the court’s required language that sealing may be vacated for cause on motion or by the court. TRO and injunction movants must show substantial efforts to contact the other side, by Rule 65 affidavit, or there will be no hearing or TRO. Arrange any bond at filing, support papers with affidavits, and be ready to argue and present witnesses immediately.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial and trial
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial and trial: Final pretrial conference: all trial counsel, the client representative, and the insurer representative, with full authority, attend in person; pending trial issues are argued and generally ruled on, and time limits may be set. Motions in limine and Daubert deadlines come in the pretrial or post-discovery order. One combined set of jury instructions (agreed instructions labeled; disputed ones with each side’s authority), with a Word copy emailed to the law clerks; separate sets are not accepted. Joint Exhibit List Chart filed and two tabbed exhibit binders (black, 3 inches maximum) delivered to chambers; plaintiffs use numbers, defendants letters. Trial Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; counsel available at 8:30 a.m. and after the jury leaves. Co-counsel may not split a witness without advance leave, Rule 50 motions must be w

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Newer lawyers
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Newer lawyers: The judge encourages newer lawyers to argue and examine witnesses and will let a more experienced lawyer assist with an examination if it doesn’t prolong the proceeding or prejudice the other side. Every attorney appearing must have authority suited to the proceeding, for example full authority on scheduling at a scheduling conference.

docs.t: Judge Robert J. Colville (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Robert J. Colville, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Extension motions are due at least 2 days before the motions deadline expires, with Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. Sentencing memoranda are expected, and Guidelines, departure, and criminal history issues go in the Position with Respect to Sentencing Factors. Travel motions must state the AUSA’s and probation officer’s positions. The government must obtain writs for in-custody defendants and give 24 hours’ notice of any bond revocation request; arrange civilian attire with the Marshal’s Office.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Motions and briefing (trap): A motion must state the specific relief and its factual and legal grounds, and affirmatively state whether it was discussed with all other parties and their positions. Every motion needs a separate proposed order detailing the relief, not just “granted.” Briefs are filed with the motion and limited to 25 pages, excluding tables. Briefs are not required for discovery motions, extensions, or continuances; the scheduling order forms list similar no-brief motions (including amendments, supplemental pleadings, substitution, and, in the initial order, motions to compel). Responses are generally due in 21 days for dispositive motions and 14 days for non-dispositive motions. The standing order says replies to dispositive motions are due within 7 days but also that replies (other than to Local Rule 56.D submissions) and sur-replies

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Rule 12 motions: meet and confer (trap): Before any Rule 12 motion, the movant must confer with opposing counsel on whether the defects can be cured, and a motion to dismiss must include a certificate of good-faith efforts to confer.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Routine motions and continuances
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Routine motions and continuances: For routine motions (amendment, extensions, continuances), seek consent and state whether it was obtained. A motion to continue a proceeding must propose at least 2 dates and times near the original date when all counsel are available.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Communications and phone appearances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Communications and phone appearances (trap): Communicate by motion, not letters; no correspondence to the judge unless requested. Law clerks may be contacted on administrative matters, including status, but not the merits. To appear by phone, fax a request to (814) 691-6001 at least 2 days before the conference; no response means it is approved. Status, initial scheduling, and post-discovery conferences may be by phone; settlement and final pretrial conferences may not unless ordered. Counsel call chambers at (814) 691-6297 only once all parties are on the line.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Discovery: If a dispute survives a good-faith conference (which the party seeking intervention must initiate promptly), contact chambers for a telephonic conference; no discovery motions until after it. Refusing to confer may draw Rule 37(a)(5) sanctions. The initial scheduling order includes a clawback procedure: the producing party must move within 30 days of notice if the privilege claim is disputed, and inadvertent disclosure is not a waiver under Fed. R. Evid. 502(d).

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Scheduling and settlement
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Scheduling and settlement: Seven days before the Post-Discovery Status Conference, the parties must jointly submit a proposed Final Scheduling Order with dates for dispositive motions, pretrial statements, motions in limine, Daubert motions and argument, the final pretrial conference, and trial. Counsel must obtain settlement authority before status conferences and are encouraged to bring principals. An insurer representative with full, unilateral settlement authority must attend any ADR session in person if insurance could cover any part of a settlement or verdict.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Per the Final Scheduling Order form, no briefing beyond the motion and response without leave. File a separate “Concise Statement of Undisputed Material Facts” strictly under Local Rule 56.B; the opponent files a paragraph-by-paragraph response under Local Rule 56.C, with additional facts in a “New Matter” section, which the movant may answer. Uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial (trap): Exhibits not identified in the pretrial narrative statement (other than impeachment exhibits) will not be admitted, and pretrial statements cannot be amended without leave. The absence of a witness is not cause to delay trial. A motion in limine requires a certificate of conference stating the exact time and place of the conference. At the pretrial conference, be ready to state exhibit objections, designate and counter-designate deposition pages and lines, estimate trial length, and have clients present or available by phone.

docs.t: Judge Stephanie L. Haines (W.D. Pa.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Stephanie L. Haines, W.D. Pa.. Oral argument: Requests are considered case by case; the court will likely allow argument if an associate or more junior attorney argues.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Deadlines without briefing orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Deadlines without briefing orders (trap): No separate briefing order generally issues, and awaiting one is no excuse. Responses to non-dispositive motions are due in 10 calendar days; responses to Rule 12 motions in 20 calendar days, with replies 5 calendar days later. Summary judgment oppositions are due in 30 calendar days and replies (including responses to new facts in the responsive concise statement) in 14 calendar days. Reconsideration motions are due within 10 calendar days, with responses 10 calendar days later.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions to dismiss (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions to dismiss (trap): Meet and confer before a Rule 12(b) motion about whether amendment can cure the defect (including with pro se parties, but not incarcerated pro se litigants). A motion without a certificate of conferral is summarily denied, and one filed without a brief is summarily dismissed. Briefs are capped at 25 pages; replies allowed without leave for Rule 12(b) and 12(c), capped at 5 pages and limited to new matters. Partial motions to dismiss do not excuse filing an answer. Parties should try not to oppose timely early motions to amend.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Motions generally
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Motions generally: Every motion needs a separate proposed order stating the specific relief. Briefs are filed with the motion, except for discovery, extension, and continuance motions. Incorporating earlier briefs is prohibited. Double-spaced, at least 12-point font, paginated. Hyperlinks to CM/ECF filings, exhibits, and Westlaw are strongly encouraged (except for pro se parties); links to sealed documents, other websites, or audio/video are prohibited, and cited websites must be attached as dated PDFs. No paper courtesy copies. Oral argument only on selected complex matters, by order; there is no set motion day. Don’t send correspondence to the judge unless requested. Conferences may be rescheduled by phone to the deputy clerk only with all counsel on the line.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Summary judgment: Strict compliance with Local Rule 56. Briefs are capped at 25 pages (excluding exhibits and concise statements) and replies at 5 pages; surreplies only with leave. The argument must cite current Supreme Court and Third Circuit authority establishing the elements of each claim. Responses to the concise statement must reprint each original fact followed by the response, seriatim. Concise statements and responses have no page limit; supporting documents go in an appendix.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes: After conferring, file an extremely brief motion, with no supporting brief and the discovery at issue attached, and call chambers so the deputy can schedule a conference. Noncompliance means denial without prejudice. Discovery motions and motions in limine require a certificate of conferral; email exchanges are not enough. Disputes during depositions may be raised by a joint call. Discovery runs 150 days if the parties choose mediation or early neutral evaluation and 120 days for arbitration. Dispositive motions and ADR do not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Remote appearances, extensions, and ADR: Requests to participate in a conference by phone must be made by motion more than 2 business days before it, for good cause. Extension and continuance motions must state supporting facts and opposing counsel’s position, suggest alternative dates when all parties are available, and be filed more than 2 business days before the deadline. File an ADR stipulation naming a proposed neutral before the initial case management conference; if the parties can’t agree, the court chooses.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement authority (trap)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Settlement authority (trap): In jury cases, counsel and persons with ultimate settlement authority (including knowledgeable insurer representatives) must attend settlement conferences, including the final pretrial conference, in person. Sanctions may follow if the person present lacks full authority; phone participation only rarely, with prior leave for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Pretrial: Post-discovery status conference after fact discovery; a final status conference after dispositive rulings, preceded by a settlement meet-and-confer. The final pretrial conference is held immediately before trial. Submit a single agreed set of jury instructions and verdict form using Third Circuit model instructions; for disputed ones, each side submits its version with authority. In bench trials, file numbered proposed findings and conclusions and a supporting brief of up to 20 pages within 20 days after trial, plus editable word-processing copies. Submit a joint glossary of technical terms, if needed, 3 business days before trial. Exhibits are marked P and D and listed in the pretrial narrative statements; get approval in advance for demonstratives in opening.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — Trial (Erie)
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. Trial (Erie): Trial generally runs Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The court conducts preliminary voir dire; jurors may take notes. Only one attorney per party may examine a given witness. Tell the court in advance about video testimony (not filed with the clerk) and test it on the court’s equipment at least a week before trial. Counsel must be reachable in person or by phone during deliberations. Notify the court before interviewing jurors.

docs.t: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter (W.D. Pa.) — R&R objections and TROs
docs.x: Judge Susan Paradise Baxter, W.D. Pa.. R&R objections and TROs: Objection briefs of 10 pages or less are encouraged. New authority or evidence not given to the magistrate judge will not be considered without a reason for the omission. No TRO if the other side has been served, if the motion lacks a certification that prompt service can’t be made, or if it lacks a Rule 65(b)(1)(A) affidavit or verified complaint. Support and responses must include affidavits.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Certificate of conferral (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Certificate of conferral (trap): Every motion must attach, as a separate exhibit, a Certificate of Conferral detailing the efforts to resolve the matter and stating whether each other party consents or opposes and whether it will file a response. A missing certificate can get the motion stricken or summarily denied, with possible sanctions. Conferral must include a verbal discussion (phone, video, or in person) on the merits; exchanging emails or letters, or leaving a voicemail the evening before or the day of filing, does not count. Counsel must also confer verbally before any conference with the court so that no one is surprised by another party’s position.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Motions and page limits (trap): Motions must state the specific relief and its factual and legal grounds, with a proposed order filed as a separate attachment stating the specific relief (not “the motion is granted”). Communicate with the court by motion, not email or letter, unless asked. No brief is needed for discovery motions or extension or continuance motions. Dispositive and class certification briefs: 25 pages (replies 15). All other motion briefs: 10 pages (replies 5). Any other written submission: 5 pages. Overlong filings may be stricken. No courtesy copies of anything on CM/ECF unless requested. Oral argument at the court’s discretion; a request should briefly explain why argument would help.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Response deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Response deadlines (trap): Responses: 21 days for motions to dismiss and to compel arbitration; 30 days for summary judgment and class certification; 5 days for discovery and case management motions (such as extensions or rescheduling); 7 days for all other motions. The 2026 version shortens the general deadline from 21 days in the 2021 version. Replies without leave within 7 days of the response (14 days for summary judgment and class certification). Sur-replies are disfavored and need leave. Motions for reconsideration are due within 7 days of the order. For urgent motions, say so in the motion and phone chambers and all counsel. Stipulations to change response times are not a substitute for a motion and court approval.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion may be filed until Judge Hardy holds an informal phone conference and grants leave. After conferring in good faith, the parties jointly contact Courtroom Deputy Kallie Sheets (412-208-7570, Kallie_sheets@pawd.uscourts.gov) with a jointly proposed agenda that fairly identifies the disputed issues. If leave is granted, the response is due within 5 days, replies are typically not permitted, and rulings often come within 7 days. During depositions, the attorneys together may call to see if the court will resolve a dispute then. Discovery ordinarily runs 150 days; any variance must be raised in the Rule 26(f) report and at the initial conference. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Extensions (trap): Extension motions must state all opposing counsel’s positions (and whether they will oppose in writing), list prior extensions, attach a proposed order and Certificate of Conferral, and be titled (with matching docket text) like “[First] Motion for [Un/Contested] Extension of Discovery” or “[First] Motion to Modify Case Management Order.” File at least 5 business days before the deadline when practicable. A first reasonable discovery extension is routinely granted if the motion describes discovery done to date and the specific discovery planned, with a tentative schedule. Don’t assume joint requests will be granted, especially late ones, and don’t informally agree to work “out of time” without a court order.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Conferences and ADR
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Conferences and ADR: The court prefers in-person proceedings. Initial case management and routine civil status conferences are usually by phone; settlement conferences, pretrial conferences, and oral arguments are in person unless permitted otherwise. Before the initial conference (usually set within 30 days after an answer), file the Rule 26(f) report and a complete Stipulation Selecting ADR Process naming the ADR type, the neutral, a confirmed session date within 60 days of the conference, and all attendees (including a representative with settlement authority). Incomplete filings may be stricken. Lead trial counsel, familiar with the case and able to stipulate, ordinarily attends conferences ready to argue pending motions and discuss settlement. A post-fact discovery status conference is usually held within 30 days after discovery closes; chambers may e

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): Leave is required for each document to be sealed. A party filing material it or another party wants sealed must first move for leave to file provisionally under seal after conferral, stating each party’s position; any party wanting the material kept sealed must then justify it item by item under In re Avandia (3d Cir. 2019). Stipulated protective orders must include the court’s required sealing provision, and the proposed sealing order must include language allowing it to be vacated for cause. Redacting personal identifiers under LR 5.2 needs no leave.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — TROs and injunctions
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. TROs and injunctions: The movant must show by Rule 65(b) affidavit serious efforts to contact the other side and why notice should not be required, or there will be no hearing or TRO. Have any bond arranged at filing. Motions and responses need supporting affidavits and proposed findings and conclusions on the court’s schedule. Be ready to proceed immediately and to choose a neutral for expedited ADR before a preliminary injunction hearing.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Settlement
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Settlement: In jury cases the court may require confidential position letters (salient facts, strengths and weaknesses, settlement posture), emailed to chambers and not filed or shared. A judicial settlement conference order typically requires an exchange of written demand and offer, a joint proposed settlement agreement with a statement of key disagreements, and ex parte position letters.

docs.t: Judge W. Scott Hardy (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge W. Scott Hardy, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: Before seeking more time for pretrial motions, confer and state whether the government consents; include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language. A pre-plea presentence report requires the defendant’s written consent and Rule 32(e)(1) waiver in the form set out in the procedures. Travel motions must state the positions of the government and Probation/Pretrial Services. After pretrial motions are decided, defense counsel should be ready to tell the court at a status conference whether the defendant will plead or go to trial.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Communications with chambers
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Communications with chambers: Communicate with the court by motion with a proposed order; no correspondence unless the court requests or approves it. Administrative (not merits) questions, including status inquiries, may go, preferably by email, to Deputy Clerk Elizabeth Abbott (Elizabeth_Abbott@pawd.uscourts.gov) or Career Law Clerk Rebecca Good McBride (Rebecca_McBride@pawd.uscourts.gov). Scheduling emails go to the deputy clerk. Emergency or time-sensitive filings: email electronic courtesy copies to both the career law clerk and the deputy clerk immediately after filing on CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Motions (trap): A motion must state in short and plain form the specific relief, the factual and legal grounds, and whether it was discussed with all other parties and their positions. Attach only the evidentiary materials necessary to decide it, plainly marked. File a proposed order stating the specific relief as a separate attachment; “the motion is granted” orders are not sufficient. For routine motions (leave to amend, extensions, continuances), confer to seek consent and state whether consent was obtained.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Briefs and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Briefs and page limits (trap): No briefs on motions for extension of time or continuance, and none on discovery disputes unless the court directs after a telephonic status conference. Dispositive motions: principal and opposition briefs 20 pages (excluding tables), replies 15. All other motions: 10 pages, replies 5, absent leave.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Oral argument: Motions are decided with or without argument at the court’s discretion. A party wanting argument must meet and confer, then the parties may file a joint motion explaining why argument would help.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Discovery disputes (trap): After a good-faith conference fails, the parties jointly email the deputy clerk to schedule a telephonic status conference. No discovery motions until after that conference, except emergencies certified by counsel. No court reporter unless requested.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Case management conferences
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Case management conferences: The telephonic Initial Case Management Conference is generally set after the answer. Before it, file the Rule 26(f) report and a fully completed Stipulation Selecting ADR Process; failure may lead the court to strike the 26(f) report. Be ready for substantive discussion; off the record unless a reporter is requested. A post-discovery status conference is held no more than 30 days after discovery closes to set summary judgment deadlines or a trial date, followed by a Pretrial Order. A final pretrial/settlement conference precedes trial; all participating trial counsel must attend.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Trial: Trial runs Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with a conference with counsel at 8:00 a.m. on evidentiary issues; counsel must notify all parties of the need for one. The court will not delay trial for last-minute conference requests that could have been raised at the morning conference. Jurors may take notes on court-provided paper and get the final instructions and admitted exhibits during deliberations. Counsel may leave the courthouse during deliberations but must be reachable by phone and able to return within ten minutes.

docs.t: Judge William S. Stickman IV (W.D. Pa.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge William S. Stickman IV, W.D. Pa.. Criminal cases: No special rules on guilty pleas or plea-agreement deadlines; early plea discussions encouraged. Before seeking more time for pretrial motions, confer for consent, state the result, and include Speedy Trial Act exclusion language in the proposed order. Pretrial motions are decided with or without a hearing; note in the motion if a hearing would help. Two formal pretrial conferences once trial is set; the civil trial procedures apply. No separate hearing on PSR objections unless requested. Tentative findings on disputed guideline issues are provided before sentencing, and notice is given of any departure ground not already identified, but the court will not reveal its position on a requested variance in advance.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motions (motions to compel, for protective order, or for sanctions) without the court’s prior permission. First confer by telephone or in person; letters, emails, or faxes do not satisfy the duty unless repeated attempts to talk fail because of the adversary’s conduct. If unresolved, e-file a Consolidated/Joint Discovery Statement: 6 pages for 4 or fewer issues, 10 pages for 5–10 issues, 12 pages for more than 10. For each issue, give Party A’s position, Party B’s response, and Party A’s reply. Attach only an excerpt of the specific disputed requests (and, if needed, responses), not the entire set; no other exhibits without permission. The court decides on the papers or sets a conference, which is recorded by a court reporter. Boilerplate objections (privilege, work product, overbroad, unduly burdensome, irrelevant)

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Record citations must appear in the brief itself, not just in the statement of facts, and each must be followed immediately by the paragraph number of the corresponding statement of fact; deposition cites need page and line. File the complete transcript of each deposition cited in the brief as a separate docket entry. Do not file the original or deliver paper copies to chambers. In responding to a statement of material facts, copy each numbered statement into the response and answer immediately below it. File in text-searchable PDF; nonconforming statements may be returned for revision.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions, page limits, and proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Extensions, page limits, and proposed orders (trap): Extensions require a motion; even joint, unopposed, or consent motions are not granted as a matter of course. Explain with specificity the unforeseen circumstances, give a timetable for finishing, state whether opposing counsel consents, and attach a proposed order. Motions to exceed page limits must be filed at least 5 days before the filing deadline. One filed with the brief will be denied absent a compelling and unanticipated reason, and arguments in excess pages will not be considered. Consent, unopposed, and joint motions must attach a proposed order granting the motion as an exhibit. Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R, and responses, are limited to 15 pages absent permission and must follow LR 5.1 formatting.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Oral argument: Motions are usually decided without argument. A request must state why argument would help and which issues it would address. The court will consider granting argument on a contested, substantive motion if an attorney less than 5 years out of law school will argue at least one substantial issue.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies: Courtroom Deputy Clerk Michelle Beck (404-215-1524, Michelle_Beck@gand.uscourts.gov) is the point of contact; calls may take up to 24 hours to return. Do not discuss the merits with the deputy or law clerks, and make all requests for court action by motion, not letter (LR 7.4). No paper courtesy copies, except for emergency motions under LR 7.2(B). Leaves of absence must be e-filed, not mailed or delivered to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Sealing and TROs
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Sealing and TROs: The court generally seals only items listed in Standing Order 04-02 and will not allow sealed filings without a court order, even on consent. Follow Section II(J) of Appendix H to the Civil Local Rules. TRO and preliminary-injunction requests must be made by separate motion under Rule 65; a request only in the complaint is not considered until the merits. After filing, contact the deputy to request expedited consideration, or the motion is treated as non-emergency.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial conference and motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial conference and motions in limine: Counsel (not parties) attend a pretrial conference, usually within 2 weeks before trial. Plaintiff’s counsel must arrange a meeting at least 10 days before it to discuss settlement and stipulate to facts and issues. Motions in limine are due 21 days before the pretrial conference, responses 9 days after the motion, and replies 5 days after the response; the court usually hears them after the pretrial conference. Be ready to identify case-in-chief witnesses. Number exhibits separately and sequentially; do not group them by category (e.g., “hospital records”).

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Jury selection and charge
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Jury selection and charge: Voir dire questions are filed as the pretrial order directs (LR 16.4). The court asks qualifying questions, jurors answer a printed background questionnaire aloud, and counsel then ask approved questions; cause challenges are heard after all questioning, followed by a 15-minute break before strikes. Civil juries: 8 jurors for trials of a week or less, more for longer trials, and no alternates. Requests to charge are due by 9:00 a.m. on the first day of trial, with a Word version emailed to the deputy the same day. Use Eleventh Circuit Pattern Instructions, then O’Malley (5th ed.), and state pattern instructions for state law; one numbered request per page with authority at the bottom, covering all substantive law.

docs.t: Judge Eleanor L. Ross (N.D. Ga.) — Trial logistics
docs.x: Judge Eleanor L. Ross, N.D. Ga.. Trial logistics: Ask permission before approaching a witness or the bench. Bringing exhibits boxes, laptops, projectors, or other trial equipment into the courthouse requires a court order; file a motion with proposed order at least 3 business days before the hearing or trial. Contact the deputy to test courtroom technology.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Discovery disputes (trap): Do not file a motion to compel, to quash, for protective order, or for sanctions without a prior conference with the court. After conferring in good faith, the movant emails Courtroom Deputy Brittany Poley (copying all counsel) a one-page summary of the dispute and relief sought, flagging any urgency, and quoting the disputed interrogatory or request. The deputy sets the briefing method (generally short emailed statements) and, if helpful, a conference recorded by a court reporter. Non-party disputes (e.g., subpoenas) follow the same procedure, and the party must tell the non-party about it. During depositions, call the court (404-215-1514 or 404-215-1510) for disputes the parties cannot resolve; for obstruction or Rule 30(d) issues, promptly set up a conference call rather than a later motion.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery responses (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Discovery responses (trap): No “Preamble” or “General Objections” sections; the court disregards them. Each request must get only the specific objections that actually apply. A party that objects and then responds must say whether the response is complete; “subject to and without waiving” answers are not allowed without that statement. Initial disclosures may not be reserved for later supplementation. Serve discovery early enough that responses are due within the discovery period; evidence requested and not produced in discovery is excluded at trial. Produce documents Bates-numbered and labeled by request or in a format showing which request each answers. Privilege claims need particulars (date, author, recipients, subject, purpose).

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions, page limits, and stipulations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Extensions, page limits, and stipulations (trap): Parties may not stipulate to extensions of time or extra pages; a motion is required. Even joint or consent extension motions are not granted as a matter of course and must explain the unforeseen circumstances, give a timetable, state opposing counsel’s position, and attach a proposed order. Motions to exceed page limits are due at least 5 days before the filing deadline; one filed with the brief is denied absent a compelling, unanticipated reason, and excess pages are not considered. Discovery extension motions must be filed before the period ends and state the original and current dates, the number of prior requests and their outcomes, and the adversary’s position (LR 26.2B). Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R, and responses, are limited to 15 pages.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Briefs and filings
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Briefs and filings: Citations go in the text in Bluebook Bluepages form, not in footnotes or endnotes. Title briefs on CM/ECF as “Brief in Support of [motion],” “[Respondent]’s Response in Opposition to [motion],” and “Reply in Support of [motion].” Surreplies are not filed in the normal course. Label uploaded exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. A: Smith Deposition”). Consent, unopposed, and joint motions must include a proposed order. Courtesy copies are not required; if sent, they must bear the CM/ECF header. Leaves of absence must be e-filed, not sent to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Record citations belong in the brief, not just the statement of facts. Cite previously docketed documents by docket number and the ECF-stamped page (e.g., “Dkt. No. [100] at 20”); deposition cites need page and line. Attach only the cited deposition pages to the brief; file the full transcript separately under a notice of filing original deposition transcript. Responses to a statement of material facts must copy each numbered statement and answer immediately below it; a reply to additional facts must copy the original statement and the response. File in text-searchable PDF; nonconforming statements are returned for revision.

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Oral argument: Motions are usually decided without argument (LR 7.1(E)); a request must state why argument would help and which issues it would address. The court will grant argument on a contested substantive motion if a lawyer less than 5 years out of law school will conduct the argument (or a large majority of it).

docs.t: Judge Leigh Martin May (N.D. Ga.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Leigh Martin May, N.D. Ga.. Material is ordinarily confidential only if it is a trade secret, personal identifying information, or HIPAA-protected health information; over-designation can draw sanctions. Any proposed protective order must include the court’s required provision that confidential material filed or used at a hearing or trial keeps protection only by complying with the Procedures for Electronic Filing Under Seal in Civil Cases. Outside hearings and trial, the court generally seals only items listed in Standing Order 04-02. Consult the designating party first about less restrictive measures, seal or redact only specific portions, and expect material used in open court not to be sealed absent extraordinary circumst

Produced documents must be Bates-numbered and tied to the requests. Video or audio footage of the subject of the dispute (e.g., body camera, surveillance, cell phone video) must be produced with initial disclosures or within 14 days after discovery of it. Initial disclosures may not be reserved for later supplementation. Boilerplate and general objections are disregarded; object specifically to each request, and say whether a response given “subject to” objections is complete. Generalized cross-references (such as to a deposition) are not acceptable interrogatory answers. docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Extensions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Extensions and page limits (trap): Parties may not stipulate to extensions or extra pages; file a motion before the deadline explaining the unforeseen circumstances, with a timetable, and note any opposition. Extensions are not granted as a matter of course, even by consent. Motions to extend discovery must be filed before the period expires and state: the original and current dates, prior requests and their outcomes, the opponent’s position and reasons, discovery taken so far, why more time is needed, and a timetable. Private agreements to extend discovery are not enforced. Page-limit extension motions are due at least 5 days before the filing deadline; one filed with the brief is denied, and overlong filings may be rejected. Objections to a magistrate judge’s R&R and responses are limited to 15 pages.

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Motions practice
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Motions practice: Title briefs on CM/ECF as “Brief in Support of …,” “Response in Opposition to …,” “Reply in Support of …,” and (only with leave) “Surreply to ….” Label exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. 1 – Smith Deposition”); with more than 25 exhibits, file a summary chart listing each with its docket number. Bluebook citations go in the text, not footnotes; noncompliant filings may be rejected. Consent, unopposed, and joint motions must attach a proposed order. TRO or injunction requests need a separate motion with evidence. An amended complaint filed as of right in response to a motion to dismiss moots any pending Rule 12 motion or request for preliminary injunctive relief. Motions are usually decided without argument; a request on a contested substantive motion will be granted if a lawyer less than 5 years out of law school will argue.

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment (trap): Statements of material facts are limited to 50 facts, with no subparts, absent approval. Before filing the brief, file the complete transcript of each cited deposition on the docket; do not attach transcripts to the brief. Record citations belong in the brief itself, with docket numbers where possible and page and line for depositions. Responses to a statement of facts must copy each numbered statement and respond immediately after it; replies copy the statement and response. File text-searchable PDFs.

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Chambers contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Chambers contact and courtesy copies: Courtroom Deputy Uzma Wiggins is the main contact, by email (TRJ_CRD@gand.uscourts.gov) or in writing. Do not discuss the merits with chambers or ask when a motion will be ruled on; no ex parte communications. No courtesy copies unless requested; if requested, hand-deliver single-sided copies printed from CM/ECF with the blue header to Room 2142. Daily or rough-draft transcripts require contacting chambers at least 2 weeks before the proceeding. Leaves of absence must be e-filed; mailed copies are not considered.

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Sealing and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Sealing and protective orders: The court disfavors broad confidentiality designations and will not approve consent protective orders that conflict with its sealing views. Material is ordinarily confidential only if it is a trade secret, personal identifying information, or HIPAA-protected health information; over-designation may be sanctioned. Protective orders must include the Guidelines’ required paragraph tying confidential status in court filings to the court’s Procedures for Electronic Filing Under Seal. Before moving to seal, consult the designating party about less restrictive options; seal or redact only specific portions, and expect no sealing of material used in open court absent extraordinary circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial (trap): Motions in limine are due at least 14 days before the pretrial conference and oppositions at least 7 days before. Plaintiff’s counsel must arrange a meeting at least 10 days before the conference to discuss settlement and stipulate facts. Bring the proposed pretrial order and any outstanding motions to the conference. Daubert motions are due by the date the proposed pretrial order is filed (LR 26.2C), with oppositions 14 days later and replies 7 days after that. A Daubert hearing is often held at the pretrial conference, so challenged experts should be ready to testify. Exhibit and witness lists, on AO Form 187, must be exchanged at least 30 days before trial. A unified set of proposed jury instructions is due 3 days after the pretrial conference, with a Word copy emailed to the deputy; supplemental charges need leave. Email proposed f

docs.t: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson (N.D. Ga.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Tiffany R. Johnson, N.D. Ga.. Trial: Court usually sits 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., with 5 to 6 hours of testimony a day. Proposed voir dire is filed with the pretrial order; jurors answer a printed questionnaire, then counsel ask approved questions, with cause challenges heard at the end and a 15-minute break before strikes. One attorney per witness objects, stating only the legal basis. Exhibit notebooks for the bench are ordinarily provided on the first day; confer with the deputy beforehand. The jury is ordinarily charged before closing arguments. A court order is required to bring exhibit boxes, laptops, projectors, or other equipment into the courthouse; move at least 3 business days ahead, naming the equipment and the people bringing it. Parties generally will not be allowed personal electronics, and trial will not be delayed for technical failures.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Contact and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Contact and courtesy copies: Courtroom Deputy Sherri Lundy is the principal contact, preferably by email (Sherri_Lundy@gand.uscourts.gov; 404-215-1481); do not discuss the merits with the deputy or the law clerks. No ex parte contact except on scheduling and procedure; requests for action must be made by motion. Courtesy copies are required only for LR 7.2(B) emergency motions and TRO or preliminary injunction motions, sent by regular mail to Ms. Lundy; courtesy copies of summary judgment motions with voluminous exhibits may be submitted. Proposed orders are required for all consent, unopposed, or joint motions. Daily or rough-draft transcripts must be requested from court reporter Geraldine Glover at least two weeks before the proceeding.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Oral argument (trap): The court will grant a request for oral argument on a contested, substantive motion if the request states that a lawyer less than seven years out of law school will argue at least one substantial issue. Motions to dismiss and for summary judgment will be noticed for hearing at least 45 days after filing. If an amended pleading moots a motion, docket a “Withdrawal of Motion.”

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — One-motion limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. One-motion limits (trap): Without leave, no party may file more than one motion to dismiss (a new one is allowed after an amended complaint), and defendants with the same counsel must file a single joint motion. Without prior leave, only one motion for summary judgment or partial summary judgment per party, and counsel representing several parties must file one motion on behalf of all of them.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Summary judgment: Record citations belong in the brief, not just the statement of facts. Simultaneously file the original transcript of each deposition cited, cite page and line in the brief, and attach only the cited pages, not the whole transcript. A response to a statement of material facts must copy each numbered statement and respond immediately after it; a reply must copy both the statement and the response before replying. All in text-searchable PDF.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Discovery (trap): Boilerplate and general objections are prohibited and will be disregarded; object specifically to each request. A party that objects and then responds must say whether anything was withheld because of the objection (“subject to and without waiving” alone is not allowed). Serve requests so responses are due by the close of discovery; the court typically will not compel late-served requests. Identify experts early enough to be deposed within the period. Before any discovery motion, confer in good faith, then contact Ms. Lundy; ordinarily each side submits a 1–2 page letter, and the court rules on the letters, holds a call, or authorizes a motion. The court is usually available by phone for deposition disputes.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): The court disfavors consent confidentiality orders; ordinarily only trade secrets, personal identifying information, and HIPAA-protected health information are truly confidential. Any such order must include (and is deemed to include) the standing order’s language that confidential material submitted to the court keeps its status only by court order. To seal, e-file a motion listing the documents with a proposed order and provisionally file the documents under seal per Appendix H; send no paper copies. Tangible items go to Ms. Lundy in chambers with a proposed order.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Motions practice and filing format
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Motions practice and filing format: Title briefs “Brief in Support of [motion],” “[Respondent]’s Response in Opposition to [motion],” and “Reply in Support of [motion]”; surreplies only if authorized. Label uploaded exhibits by content (e.g., “Ex. A: Smith Deposition”). TRO and preliminary injunction requests must be by separate motion (not in the complaint); then contact Ms. Lundy for expedited consideration or a hearing. File leaves of absence on the docket only; they are not automatically granted. Request a conference with the court through Ms. Lundy when counsel has specific goals and an agenda.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Pretrial (trap): If a summary judgment motion is pending, the consolidated pretrial order is ordinarily due 30 days after the ruling unless a date is set. Plaintiffs cannot enlarge or change their claims in the pretrial order over objection. Witness and exhibit lists cannot reserve a right to supplement or adopt another party’s list; unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent manifest injustice. Motions in limine and Daubert motions at least 14 days before the pretrial conference, responses 7 days before. Proposed findings and conclusions must also be sent to the law clerk in text-searchable PDF. Anyone without a blue attorney ID card needs a proposed order, at least 3 business days ahead, to bring laptops or camera phones into the courthouse.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Jury selection
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Jury selection: Civil trials up to 2 weeks normally seat 8 jurors with no alternates (possibly 7 for trials under a week) from a panel of 20; alert the court promptly if a larger panel is needed, such as for media attention or a mutual insurer. After the court’s qualifying questions, counsel conduct general voir dire of the panel and then question each juror individually. Cause motions follow outside the jury’s presence; each side gets 3 peremptory strikes, alternating on a strike sheet starting with plaintiff.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Trial: Court usually sits 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; counsel present at 9:00 a.m. Expect 5 to 6 hours of testimony per day. Openings are generally limited to 20 minutes and closings to 30 minutes per side; seek more time at the pretrial conference. Before trial, give the deputy a notebook of pre-marked exhibits for the judge and file witness and numbered exhibit lists; hand the court small copies of enlarged boards. No permission is needed to approach a witness with an exhibit. Only the examining attorney may object, stating only the legal basis; one attorney per party at the charge conference. Speak from a microphone; no motions in the jury’s presence, though mistrial motions must be made immediately.

docs.t: Judge William M. Ray II (N.D. Ga.) — Jury charges
docs.x: Judge William M. Ray II, N.D. Ga.. Jury charges: File, and email to the deputy in Word, a single unified set of proposed instructions no later than the morning of the first day of trial, showing for disputed charges the proponent, the legal basis, and the opposition’s basis. Supplemental charges require oral leave and are not accepted later than a day before the end of trial absent manifest justice.

docs.t: Judge Adrienne Nelson (D. Or.) — Judge’s copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Judge’s copies (trap): Parties are exempt from Local Rule 5-10 paper filing, except for documents identified in the Trial Management Order. Do not send paper courtesy copies; the judge reads filings electronically.

docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Proposed orders and jury instructions: Submit jury instructions and proposed forms of order under LR 5 to the chambers proposed-document email address linked on the page. It may not be used for filings, and unauthorized correspondence is deleted.

docs.t: Judge Adrienne Nelson (D. Or.) — Young lawyers
docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Young lawyers: The judge encourages giving lawyers practicing less than 7 years substantive speaking roles, including oral argument and witness examination, especially where they drafted or significantly contributed to the briefing. An experienced attorney may supplement their argument or questioning if necessary.

docs.t: Judge Adrienne Nelson (D. Or.) — Briefs
docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Briefs: The court strongly encourages hyperlinking cited cases in briefs (see Section 5 of the CM/ECF User Manual).

docs.t: Judge Adrienne Nelson (D. Or.) — Expedited case management
docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Expedited case management: If the parties agree to an expedited trial schedule, the court will hold a case management conference on discovery limits and the need for dispositive motions, and will make every effort to set trial within six months of that conference.

docs.t: Judge Adrienne Nelson (D. Or.) — Courtroom rules
docs.x: Judge Adrienne Nelson, D. Or.. Courtroom rules: Wireless devices on silent in the courthouse. No recording at any time in the courthouse or during any remote proceeding (telephone, video, or other electronic means). Give advance notice if you need teleconferencing, the courtroom video displays, or other presentation technology. Refer to parties by their proper names (“Mr. Smith,” not “the defendant”) during argument and testimony; decorum and civility are expected.

docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Judge’s copies (trap): Judge Baggio expects compliance with LR 5-8(a): a fastened paper copy marked “JUDGE’S COPY,” with the Notice of Electronic Filing, delivered to the Clerk’s Office within 3 business days for dispositive and injunctive motions (and all related papers), Social Security records, and any filing over 10 pages in the aggregate. On objections to a Findings and Recommendation, give copies of the objection and response only. For trial documents, paper judge’s copies are due at the Clerk’s Office the same day as filing, double-sided and three-hole punched; in criminal cases this applies to ALL pretrial documents regardless of length.

docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Do not file proposed orders or judgments in ECF (except protective and pretrial orders) unless the court asks; if requested, email them in Word.

docs.t: Judge Amy M. Baggio (D. Or.) — Protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Protective orders (trap): Use Judge Baggio’s own modified Tier 2 stipulated protective order template, not the district’s model. Any changes require filing two versions, one clean and one with tracked edits against the judge’s template, plus an explanation of why the case needs a different approach. The judge’s template bars submitting designated material to any public generative AI tool (e.g., ChatGPT), even if anonymized. Designation disputes go first to conferral, then by email to the courtroom deputy with a one-page letter per party; the court decides whether a motion is needed. A non-designating party files designated material under seal; if it asks in writing to unseal, the designating party has 10 calendar days to move to keep it sealed or the court unseals it.

docs.t: Judge Amy M. Baggio (D. Or.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Criminal cases: Motions to continue trial are due 4 weeks before trial. Supervised release violation submissions are due from both sides 3 business days before the hearing. The USMS transport list is prepared the Monday before the next week’s hearings, so tell the court of date changes or the defendant may be transported. Contact the deputy at least 6 weeks before trial so a jury can be summoned. Parties secure their own interpreters for witnesses. 28 days before the pretrial conference, notify the deputy whether the case is going to trial; if not, set a plea hearing (plea agreement and petition due by noon the day before) or move to continue. A continuance motion must state prior continuances, a proposed date with detailed reasons, the defendant’s custody location, client consent and Speedy Trial waiver (excluding time 30 days beyond the new date), and all p

docs.t: Judge Amy M. Baggio (D. Or.) — Criminal trial filings
docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Criminal trial filings: 28 days before the pretrial conference: motions in limine, trial memoranda, joint jury instructions (also emailed in Word), voir dire, exhibit list, expert list and summaries, proposed verdict form (also in Word), and the government’s complete witness list. Responses and objections are due 21 days before. Instructions must include a draft set of “Pre-Opening Statement Instructions” (presumption of innocence, burden, charges, and elements); the court expects to resolve all instruction objections before openings. The defendant need not disclose exhibits in advance. For Daubert challenges, contact the deputy to set a briefing schedule and hearing. Revised exhibit list and JERS USB drive are due by close of business 2 days after the pretrial conference.

All motions in limine go in one document of no more than 20 pages; responses in one document of no more than 15 pages. Conferral is required. Daubert motions are filed separately on a deadline set at the trial scheduling conference. Jury instructions must be complete with no placeholders, indexed, and page-broken; for

docs.x: Judge Amy M. Baggio, D. Or.. Exhibits and witnesses: Plaintiff uses yellow stickers starting at 1, defendant blue starting at 501, with the case number on each sticker and every exhibit paginated; strip discovery numbering. Provide the court both double-sided tabbed binders and a thumb drive. The court generally preadmits only stipulated exhibits, and a preadmitted exhibit not used at trial is removed from evidence. An amended exhibit gets a new number at the end of the list; amended lists show removed exhibits in strikethrough and highlight new ones. 2 business days after the pretrial conference, file an updated exhibit list (columns: Pretrial Ruling, Stipulated, Preadmitted, Offered, Received), a joint witness list, an updated ruling chart, and (jury trials) a JERS thumb drive, except in Pendleton. Witnesses are expected to testify in person, subject to FRCP 43(a). Late submissions are

docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. No paper copies (trap): Parties are exempt from LR 5-8 paper filing except for documents identified in the Trial Management Order. Do not send Judge McShane paper or courtesy copies of filings.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Discovery disputes: The judge prefers to resolve discovery disputes informally by phone rather than by motion. Email the courtroom deputy an outline of the dispute and each side’s position; a phone conference is set within days.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Oral argument and remote appearances
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Oral argument and remote appearances: Requests for oral argument are granted in most cases. Video hearings may be set for out-of-town counsel on request, and if one side appears by video, both sides will be asked to.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Scheduling
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Scheduling: Rule 16 conferences are set after all defendants answer. Confer on a discovery plan beforehand and have calendars available for discovery and dispositive motion deadlines. After dispositive motions are resolved (or if none are filed), a trial scheduling conference aims to set trial within 120 days. If the parties agree to an expedited schedule, the court will hold a case management conference on limiting discovery and dispositive motions and try to set trial within 6 months.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Trial management order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Trial management order deadlines: The court automatically enters a Trial Management Order 90 days before trial. Pretrial conferences are in person in Eugene. Under the sample TMO: 30 days before the pretrial conference, plaintiff’s exhibit lists and judge’s copies, witness statements and expert reports, special damages, and the pretrial order; 21 days before, defendant’s exhibits and witness materials, deposition designations, trial memoranda, voir dire, and verdict forms; 14 days before, motions in limine, rebuttal materials, and objections; 7 days before, responses. Trial memoranda are limited to 35 pages; all motions in limine and all responses each go in a single document not exceeding 35 pages, with separate motions as subparts.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Witnesses, exhibits, and depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Witnesses, exhibits, and depositions (trap): Lay witness statements must give the complete substance of testimony, not just the subject, and testimony is limited to what is stated; give direct time estimates. Expert narratives likewise limit trial testimony. Plaintiff’s exhibits start at 1, defendant’s at 201; replacements take a letter suffix. Exhibits go in three-hole-punched, tabbed binders; impeachment exhibits are sealed and delivered only to the court. Depositions used in lieu of live testimony must be submitted highlighted; shared depositions are submitted jointly with each party in a different color. Late submissions are not accepted absent a strong showing of good cause.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Jury trial practices
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Jury trial practices: The judge will consider a timing order, preliminary instructions on the law, juror questions, and mid-trial mini summations, discussed at the pretrial conference. Jury questionnaires are encouraged in long, complex cases. The judge strongly encourages giving lawyers practicing less than 7 years speaking roles in argument and witness examination, with an experienced attorney able to supplement.

docs.t: Judge Michael J. McShane (D. Or.) — Courtroom rules
docs.x: Judge Michael J. McShane, D. Or.. Courtroom rules: Turn off mobile devices. Give advance notice of teleconferencing or technology needs. Refer to parties by name (e.g., “Mr. Smith,” not “the defendant”). Do not rise when the judge enters or leaves; all rise for the jury. Counsel may sit or stand during argument. Jury instructions and proposed orders may be emailed to the chambers proposed-document address per LR 5 only; it may not be used for filings.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Rule 26(f) report replaces Rule 16 conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Rule 26(f) report replaces Rule 16 conference (trap): Within 21 days after all defendants answer, file a joint Rule 26(f) report proposing dates for close of fact and expert discovery, dispositive motions, and the joint ADR report and pretrial order. The court typically expects discovery to close within 120 days of the scheduling order and dispositive motions within 150 days; a longer proposal must explain in detail why. If the court agrees with the dates, it enters a scheduling order without a Rule 16 conference.

docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Extensions (trap): Extension motions, even unopposed, must be received at least 5 days before the current deadline (absent exigent circumstances) and explain good cause.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Discovery disputes: Formal discovery motions are discouraged. Email a brief summary of the dispute to the courtroom deputy (kasubhai_crd@ord.uscourts.gov); if email does not resolve it, an expedited telephone hearing is set.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Motions and briefs
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Motions and briefs: Hyperlink cited cases in briefs (see Section 5 of the CM/ECF User Manual). Oral argument is not automatic; the court will contact the parties if it wants argument. Seek summary judgment only on issues genuinely free of material factual dispute or raising significant dispositive legal issues. Cite declarations by paragraph and depositions by page, and submit documents in an organized fashion. Parties are exempt from LR 5-8 paper judge’s copies except for documents identified in the Trial Management Order.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Pronouns and honorifics
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Pronouns and honorifics: Parties and counsel are encouraged to give their pronouns and honorifics (Mx., Ms., Mr.), including in signature lines and pretrial witness submissions, and must address each other and witnesses accordingly in filings and proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Trial setting and pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Trial setting and pretrial filings: Trial is generally set only after dispositive motions are resolved; the trial date is firm. Pretrial conferences are generally in person. 28 days before the pretrial conference: plaintiff’s exhibit list (filed) and exhibits (to chambers, not filed), witness statements, and pretrial order. 21 days before: defendants’ equivalents, all deposition designations, trial memoranda (15 pages), verdict forms, joint and contested jury instructions (each on a separate page, modifications in bold or underline, also emailed to MKPropdoc@ord.uscourts.gov), and a joint neutral statement. 14 days before: specific motions in limine (no boilerplate motions like “preclude hearsay”), objections, and a joint list of stipulated exhibits. 7 days before: responses, plus a Word chart of all rulings needed, emailed (not e-filed) to MKPropdoc@or

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Trial practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Trial practice (trap): Attorneys, not the judge, conduct voir dire after the court’s introductory questions. Witnesses other than experts are excluded. Lay witness statements may simply say the witness will testify consistent with deposition; otherwise give the complete substance. The court does not provide translators in civil cases. Plaintiff’s exhibits start at 1 and defendants’ at 201, in tabbed three-hole binders. Deposition testimony usually does not go to the jury; the court’s clerk can serve as a proxy reader. New lawyers (under 7 years) may argue and examine witnesses with a senior attorney backing up; the court will suspend the one witness/one attorney rule.

docs.t: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai (D. Or.) — Settlement and consent
docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Settlement and consent: Request settlement conferences through the courtroom deputy; the court will help locate a settlement judge. Parties are encouraged to consider consenting to a magistrate judge, who may offer an earlier trial date.

docs.x: Judge Mustafa T. Kasubhai, D. Or.. Courtroom rules: Turn off mobile devices. Give advance notice of teleconferencing or technology needs. Pro hac vice attorneys and Oregon counsel should know the Local Rules.

docs.t: Judge Matthew E. Orso (W.D.N.C.) — Page limits and format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Page limits and format (trap): Opening and opposition memoranda: 25 pages (including caption, excluding signatures and certificates); replies: 12 pages. Don’t file an over-length brief, even as an exhibit to a motion for leave, without leave. Double space using Word’s “double spaced” setting (not 24-point spacing); all text, including footnotes, in a proportional font of at least 12-point type.

docs.t: Judge Matthew E. Orso (W.D.N.C.) — AI-generated filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. AI-generated filings (trap): An attorney (or a paralegal at the attorney’s direction, or a pro se party) must check every statement and citation for accuracy. The court may summarily strike any filing, or deny any motion, that contains hallucinated citations or assertions.

docs.t: Judge Matthew E. Orso (W.D.N.C.) — Exhibits, courtesy copies, and hearings
docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Exhibits, courtesy copies, and hearings: File all exhibits relied on, but none that the briefs don’t cite. For deposition excerpts, highlight the cited testimony in yellow and file only the pages needed for context; the court prefers one transcript page per PDF page. No courtesy copies unless memoranda or exhibits are sealed; then deliver a flash drive of the sealed documents to chambers, with file names matching their CM/ECF docket numbers. Motions are usually decided on the papers; request oral argument in the motion or response if it would help. PowerPoints are disfavored and, absent permission, limited to 15 slides, 40 or fewer words per slide, in 24-point or larger font.

docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. The motions deadline (all motions except motions in limine and to continue) can’t be extended by agreement, and stipulated discovery extensions don’t move it. The parties may consent to extend discovery only to a date at least 21 days before trial.

docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Pretrial filings (trap): Subpoena all trial witnesses at least 14 days before trial, or the court may decline to enforce or quash them. Responses to motions in limine are due in 10 days and replies in 4 days, regardless of the docket-generated date. At least 14 days before trial: joint voir dire questions, joint proposed jury instructions, and deposition designations (only for witnesses not testifying live).
