docs.t: Judge Matthew E. Orso (W.D.N.C.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Trial: By 2 p.m. two business days before trial (for example, Thursday for a Monday trial), file a witness list, expert qualifications (unless stipulated), authenticity stipulations, and an exhibit list with columns for Exhibit #, Description, Identified by, and Admitted. Provide electronic exhibits (each a separate file, named to match the exhibit list) on a CD, DVD, or flash drive for JERS, in the listed formats. A party with more than 15 documentary exhibits must bring 2 identical, individually tabbed exhibit notebooks. Video depositions must be edited for objections before trial or the objections are waived. Jury costs may be assessed equally against the parties if a jury case settles without notice to the Clerk’s Office at least one full business day before trial, or settles during trial, absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Matthew E. Orso (W.D.N.C.) — Civil jury selection and instructions
docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Civil jury selection and instructions: The court conducts voir dire using a confidential juror questionnaire and may allow counsel a short period (e.g., ten minutes). Juries are 8 with no alternates; a verdict stands with at least 6 jurors. Each side gets 3 peremptory challenges (up to 3 more in exceptional cases), exercised concurrently in writing against the 14–16 seated jurors; the first 8 unstruck jurors are seated. Instructions are given throughout trial. Request any cautionary or explanatory instruction immediately when needed during trial, or any objection to its omission is waived. Only issue instructions go to the jury room.

docs.x: Judge Matthew E. Orso, W.D.N.C.. Late motions are summarily denied. Rule 17(b) subpoena motions are due 14 days before the term. Proposed jury instructions (a single joint Word document, objections in footnotes), voir dire, and verdict sheets must be filed and emailed in Word to chambers 14 days before the term; joint voir dire and verdict sheets are not required. docs.t: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner (M.D. Ga.) — Court’s voir dire, both case types
docs.x: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner, M.D. Ga.. Court’s voir dire, both case types: The court asks about pretrial publicity and discussion of the case, whether jurors know the judge, the parties, counsel, their firms, the listed witnesses, or other panel members, and about physical limitations that would prevent sitting through trial. It also asks about court-system employment, legal training (including paralegal, forensic, and criminal justice coursework), prior testimony, and courtroom TV shows, and whether any juror cannot follow the law as charged or sit in judgment for moral or religious reasons.

docs.t: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner (M.D. Ga.) — Civil voir dire
docs.x: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner, M.D. Ga.. Civil voir dire: Fill-ins cover plaintiff, defendant, each side’s attorney, and each attorney’s firm, plus a short statement of plaintiff’s claims. Civil-specific questions cover prior lawsuits (as a party or otherwise), prior jury or grand jury service, and whether any juror could not hold for the defendant if plaintiff fails its burden or could not award money damages if plaintiff meets it.

docs.t: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner (M.D. Ga.) — Criminal voir dire
docs.x: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner, M.D. Ga.. Criminal voir dire: Fill-ins cover the defendant, defense counsel and firm, and the assigned Assistant U.S. Attorney. Criminal-specific questions cover law enforcement and corrections employment or applications (by jurors or close family), giving greater weight to government or law enforcement witnesses, unfair treatment by the criminal justice system, and crime-prevention or neighborhood-watch membership within the last 5 years. The court instructs that the defendant need not prove innocence, produce evidence, or testify, and asks whether any juror could not follow that instruction.

docs.t: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner (M.D. Ga.) — Witness lists for voir dire
docs.x: Judge Leslie Abrams Gardner, M.D. Ga.. Witness lists for voir dire: In both civil and criminal cases, the court reads the list of potential witnesses to the panel and asks whether anyone knows them.

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — Settlement and dismissal (trap)

docs.t: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon (W.D. Va.) — ERISA benefits cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Elizabeth K. Dillon, W.D. Va.. ERISA benefits cases (trap): The proposed ERISA order becomes the scheduling order unless a party objects within 10 days. Plaintiff’s brief (with any authenticity objections to the record) is due 30 days after service of the record, defendant’s response 30 days later, and an optional reply 7 days later. Oral argument must be requested promptly after the last brief by contacting Judicial Assistant Miriam Frazier (miriamf@vawd.uscourts.gov or 540-857-5120); otherwise the court rules on the papers. Deadlines may be moved by filed written stipulation, but no more than 60 days without leave.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Appearances and contact (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Appearances and contact (trap): All hearings are attended by counsel in person unless prior leave is timely sought and granted. Counsel may contact the courtroom manager (Tammy Kimura, 808-541-3073) about continuances and similar scheduling relief. Nothing may be faxed to chambers without prior permission from chambers staff.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Summary judgment (trap): Only one Rule 56 motion per party without leave, sought by noticed motion showing good cause. An early motion (for example, on immunity) followed by a later motion after more discovery is an example of good cause.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Motions in limine (trap): Due 3 weeks before trial; responses due 2 weeks before trial; no replies. No Daubert motions once trial has begun.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Electronic devices
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Electronic devices: In the courtroom, only attorneys of record may use devices, only for the ongoing case-related proceeding and with court approval. Phones off on entering the courtroom; no cameras or recording in the courtroom or chambers. The order does not authorize bringing devices to the courthouse for other matters. Violations draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Trial schedule and jury selection
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Trial schedule and jury selection: Jury trials run 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. with no lunch break (bring a snack); some days may run later. Jurors may take notes.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Exhibits and witnesses (trap)
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Exhibits and witnesses (trap): Meet and confer on a common exhibit set and try to stipulate to authenticity and admissibility; no statement of objections need be filed despite the Rule 16 order. File exhibit lists by the final pretrial conference date. Exhibits go in 3-ring binders no larger than 3 inches at the spine; one original and two copies are due the Thursday before trial. Disclose the next day’s witnesses to counsel and the court by 4:30 p.m. the prior business day; undisclosed witnesses may not testify.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Demonstratives and deposition testimony
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Demonstratives and deposition testimony: No demonstratives in opening, and no material not in evidence during examination or closing, without all parties’ consent or (failing agreement) leave of court, obtained in advance without delaying the jury. Exhibits are generally not passed among jurors. Use the microphone (lapel mics on request). For published deposition testimony, give timely notice; counsel generally meet with the court by the prior trial day to resolve objections, and the offering party provides a revised designation transcript by the start of that trial day, plus a reader if read aloud.

docs.t: Judge Derrick Watson (D. Haw.) — Jury instructions and pretrial filings
docs.x: Judge Derrick Watson, D. Haw.. Jury instructions and pretrial filings: Comply with Local Rule 51.1; L.R. 51.1(b) and (e)–(j) also apply to verdict forms. File a joint, brief, objective statement of the case for voir dire 2 weeks before trial. Counsel arrange their own interpreters well ahead, get advance permission for special equipment, and give the courtroom manager after-hours phone numbers before trial.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Summary judgment concise statements (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Summary judgment concise statements (trap): The separate concise statement is limited to 5 pages or 1500 words, includes only material facts absolutely necessary to the motion, and contains no argument. Facts in the moving party’s statement are deemed admitted unless controverted in the opposing concise statement. Support each fact with specific evidence, identifying the filing, the portion and page, and where it is found in ECF; highlight or otherwise emphasize the relevant portions. Documents need not be filed in full. File the concise statement separately, not as an attachment to the motion. All exhibits on originals and courtesy copies need labeled tabs. The memo attaches example moving and opposing statements (two-column facts and evidence format).

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Continuing trial
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Continuing trial: All motions to continue trial filed within 30 days of the trial date are heard by Judge Gillmor.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Rule 404(b) notice in criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Rule 404(b) notice in criminal cases (trap): Oral statements do not satisfy 404(b) notice in felony trials before Judge Gillmor. At the final pretrial conference before the magistrate judge, the government will be required to file and serve, within two days, written notice describing the 404(b) evidence with enough particularity for the defendant to identify the act. The defendant files and serves a written response within two days after the notice is filed.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Trial days and out-of-jury matters
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Trial days and out-of-jury matters: Jury trial sessions are Tuesday to Friday; in a week with a Monday holiday, Wednesday to Friday. At recesses and at the end of each session, once the jury leaves, the court asks whether counsel have matters for the record. Offers of proof, preservation of objections, motions to reconsider evidentiary rulings, and witness or scheduling discussions happen then.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Objections at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Objections at trial (trap): Counsel must rise and wait to be recognized before stating an objection, and state it in five words or less (for example, “Objection - Hearsay”). The court will rule, ask for a short response or explanation, or call a sidebar. No further argument in the jury’s hearing; save argument, offers of proof, and record preservation for the next recess.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Courtroom decorum (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Courtroom decorum (trap): Stand when court opens, recesses, or adjourns, when the jury enters or leaves, and when addressing or addressed by the court. Examine witnesses and give openings and closings from the lectern; approach the courtroom manager’s desk only with permission, and the bench only when invited. Address remarks to the court, refer to everyone by surname, and only one attorney per party examines or cross-examines each witness (the attorney objecting on direct handles cross). Hand unmarked papers to the courtroom manager for marking before they go to a witness, with a copy for the court, and hand offered exhibits to opposing counsel. Do not echo or thank witnesses for answers; make stipulation offers privately, not before the jury. In openings and arguments, do not express personal knowledge or opinion, read or purport to read from transcript

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Jury instructions: The judge posts general civil (2023) and criminal (2023, in female and male defendant versions that differ only in pronouns) jury instructions covering standard topics such as burden of proof, credibility, experts, impeachment, notes, outside research, deliberation, and the verdict form.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Electronic devices (trap)
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Electronic devices (trap): Under the November 6, 2008 General Order, attorneys of record may bring laptops, phones, and tablets into the courthouse only for use in case-related proceedings in the courtroom or chambers, and must tell court security at the entrance the time of their proceeding and the case name. The order does not cover paralegals, other staff, parties, or witnesses. The authorization does not apply when counsel enters for a matter other than a hearing or conference with Judge Gillmor. Cell phones must be off in the courtroom unless the court permits, and no camera or audio/video equipment may be used in hearings or chambers.

docs.t: Judge Helen W. Gillmor (D. Haw.) — Contact
docs.x: Judge Helen W. Gillmor, D. Haw.. Contact: Chambers (808) 541-3502; orders to gillmor_orders@hid.uscourts.gov. Courtroom manager Theresa Lam, (808) 541-3577, theresa_lam@hid.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Jill Otake (D. Haw.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jill Otake, D. Haw.. Contacting chambers (trap): Request any action only by filing a letter or motion; do not email or call chambers. Questions about practices: read the procedures and Local Rules first, then email otake_orders@hid.uscourts.gov copying all counsel and self-represented parties. Phone inquiries are disfavored. docs.t: Judge Jill Otake (D. Haw.) — Remote appearances
docs.x: Judge Jill Otake, D. Haw.. Remote appearances: File a letter request as soon as practicable and no later than 36 hours before the hearing. Telephonic appearances at dispositive motion hearings are disfavored. No recording by remote attendees.

docs.t: Judge Jill Otake (D. Haw.) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jill Otake, D. Haw.. Continuances (trap): Every motion-hearing continuance, even a joint one, requires a filed motion stating which number continuance it is (e.g., “First Motion to Continue …”), filed well ahead. Civil trial: a joint request more than 5 months before trial may go by stipulation to the magistrate judge showing good cause; within 5 months a motion is required. Continuances over 6 months are disfavored. State prior continuances and any deadlines to reopen or extend; proposed orders go to otake_orders@hid.uscourts.gov in Word, copying all parties. docs.x: Judge Jill Otake, D. Haw.. Motions and meet-and-confer (trap): Local Rule 7.8 conferences must be by lead counsel in real time; letters or emails do not count. docs.t: Judge Jill Otake (D. Haw.) — Chambers copies and sealing
docs.x: Judge Jill Otake, D. Haw.. Chambers copies and sealing: One chambers copy of motions, oppositions, replies, and attachments. docs.x: Judge John Michael Seabright, D. Haw.. If the defendant renews its motion, the plaintiff may not file a second amended complaint without leave.

docs.x: Judge Micah W. J. Smith, D. Haw.. If any party opposes, or trial is five months away or less, submit a stipulation or motion (with proposed order) to Judge Smith, stating the number of prior continuances and whether closed deadlines are to be reopened or current ones extended. Continuances pushing trial back more than six months are disfavored and must be justified with particularity.

docs.x: Judge Micah W. J. Smith, D. Haw.. If more time is needed, come prepared to propose how much; the court will set a motions deadline, exclude time, and usually set trial within 70 days after the motions deadline. Once the trial date is confirmed or set this way, motions to continue it are viewed with great disfavor, require a motion and proposed order, and will likely be set for hearing. Continuances based on reasons or conflicts known when the date was set are highly unlikely to be granted. docs.t: Judge Micah W. J. Smith (D. Haw.) — Settlement (trap)

docs.t: Judge Micah W. J. Smith (D. Haw.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Micah W. J. Smith, D. Haw.. Trial: Jury trials usually start on Mondays and run Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m., with breaks at about 10:30 a.m. (10 minutes), 12:00 to 12:45 p.m., and 2:30 p.m. (10 minutes). Counsel must appear at 8:45 a.m. daily and be ready to stay after 3:45 p.m.; to appear earlier, email the courtroom manager early on the preceding trial day. Bench trials generally follow the same schedule, but the judge will confer on a case-specific schedule, including unusually long or short days. To tailor a trial schedule, email the courtroom manager (copying all counsel) to request a pretrial conference. Criminal trials: the court conducts all voir dire from questions the parties submit; counsel may not question jurors directly. Civil trials: each side gets up to 20 minutes of its own voir dire, but the court conducts most of it, so submit proposed questions.

docs.t: Judge Micah W. J. Smith (D. Haw.) — Courtroom conduct and feedback
docs.x: Judge Micah W. J. Smith, D. Haw.. Courtroom conduct and feedback: Inside the courtroom only attorneys of record and their litigation team may use electronic devices, and only for the ongoing case-related proceeding; ask if in doubt. No cameras or recording equipment in the courtroom or chambers; violations draw sanctions. Parties must act with the highest professionalism, including in discovery and depositions. After a case is finally resolved, counsel may request a feedback meeting in chambers by email to smith_orders@hid.uscourts.gov; all counsel of record must participate or consent.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Contacting chambers (trap): Call or email the courtroom manager (Theresa Lam, 808-541-3577 or 808-721-2633, Theresa_Lam@hid.uscourts.gov) for procedural and scheduling matters, and respond promptly when contacted. Calls or emails directly to chambers are strongly disfavored and only for time-sensitive matters when the courtroom manager is unavailable. Otherwise communicate only by ECF filing. ECF filings are not necessarily reviewed the same day; if a matter needs immediate attention, email park_orders@hid.uscourts.gov, copying all counsel of record, or the email will not be read. No ex parte communication with the judge or staff without prior leave; violations without good cause draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Remote appearances
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Remote appearances: Virtual and telephonic appearances at hearings on dispositive or substantive motions are disfavored. Counsel or pro se parties not located on O‘ahu must email a letter request to park_orders@hid.uscourts.gov at least one week before the hearing, stating why remote appearance is warranted. Pro hac vice requests based on convenience will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Chambers copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Chambers copies and proposed orders: No more than one chambers copy of motions and attachments. None needed for civil answers, notices of appearance, motions to exceed page limits, or motions to continue; or, in criminal cases, notices of appearance, applications to appear for the United States, motions to continue a hearing or trial, and sentencing statements. Documents of 50 pages or less may be stapled; longer documents go in binders labeled “binder 1 of 3,” and so on. For referred motions, follow the magistrate judge’s rules. Stipulations and orders needing approval go to park_orders@hid.uscourts.gov in Word, with dates and electronic signatures; that address is not for general correspondence.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Motions and meet-and-confer (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Motions and meet-and-confer (trap): Local Rule 7.8 conferences must be held by lead counsel by a method allowing real-time communication; letters or emails do not count. Discuss the issues in enough detail that any remaining briefing targets only what needs resolving. Daubert motions are treated as non-dispositive and must meet the Scheduling Order deadlines; Daubert issues may not be raised in motions in limine. Motions in limine must identify the specific evidence, the grounds, and why an ordinary trial objection is inadequate. Memoranda and oppositions are limited to 5 pages (leave needed to exceed). Counsel must tell witnesses about in limine rulings and admonish them to comply.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Summary judgment (trap): One motion only: a party may not split summary judgment on several claims into multiple motions. Each fact in a concise statement must be a single sentence with a citation, in a separately numbered paragraph. The Opposing Concise Statement must be a 2-column chart repeating every moving fact (same order, numbers, and citations) beside a response stating undisputed, disputed (and why), or disputed in part (and why), with pincites (page and line where available). The movant’s Reply to Opposing Concise Statement is a 3-column chart (moving fact, opposing response, reply with pincites); landscape orientation is allowed.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Continuances (trap): Unopposed joint requests to continue a civil or criminal hearing may go through the courtroom manager; opposed requests need an ECF motion stating which number continuance it is (e.g., “Second Motion to Continue …”). Ask well ahead of the hearing. Civil trial: if trial is more than 5 months away and all agree, stipulate before the assigned magistrate judge showing good cause. If opposed, or if trial is 5 months away or less, use a stipulation (via park_orders@hid.uscourts.gov) or a motion with proposed order stating prior continuances and any deadlines to reopen or extend. Continuances of more than 6 months are disfavored and need particularized reasons. Criminal: a Rule 17.1 pretrial conference follows the initial appearance; be ready to discuss discovery, motions, and trial readiness, and any requested continuance length. Later tr

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Electronic devices
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Electronic devices: Devices must be silenced or off in the courtroom. Only attorneys of record and their litigation team may use them, and only for the ongoing case-related proceeding; ask the courtroom manager in advance if unsure. No cameras or recording equipment in the courtroom or chambers; violations draw sanctions.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Trial schedule and voir dire
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Trial schedule and voir dire: Jury trials start Tuesdays and run 9 a.m. to 2:30 or 3 p.m. (to 4:30 p.m. on jury selection days), with breaks at about 11 a.m. (15 minutes) and 12:30 p.m. (20 minutes). Counsel meet with the court daily at 8:30 a.m. or after the day ends. In civil cases the judge limits each party’s hours. Bench trials run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with lunch from noon to 1:30 p.m. The court conducts general voir dire, incorporating parties’ special questions; each side then has 20 minutes (more may be considered in complex cases).

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Trial conduct and exhibits
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Trial conduct and exhibits: Sidebars are highly discouraged; defer disputes to recess. Speak at the podium using the microphone, state only the basis of objections, and make offers of proof outside the jury’s presence. Disclose the next day’s witnesses by the close of each trial day; the exclusionary rule applies from motions/jury selection through closings. No demonstratives shown to the jury without permission or stipulation. Agree on a common exhibit set and report agreed and disputed exhibits (by number) by the motions in limine hearing. Provide one set of exhibits in separate labeled manila folders, one tabbed binder set, and JERS electronic exhibits on the same day. Exhibits are generally not passed among jurors. Motions during trial should generally be written; special equipment needs advance permission.

docs.t: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park (D. Haw.) — Jury instructions and bench trials
docs.x: Judge Shanlyn A. S. Park, D. Haw.. Jury instructions and bench trials: Instructions derived from Ninth Circuit or other model instructions must be redlined to show changes. Submit proposed instructions and special verdict forms in Word by email to park_orders@hid.uscourts.gov and on disk or thumb drive to the courtroom manager. Jurors get hard copies and may take notes. Civil bench trials: trial briefs by the Scheduling Order deadline; after ruling, the prevailing party drafts findings of fact and conclusions of law annotated to the transcript, and the other side files objections and revisions.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Appendices for evidence (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Appendices for evidence (trap): In civil cases, any evidence or factual material relied on to support or oppose a filing (depositions, documents, ESI, affidavits, declarations, stipulations, admissions, interrogatory answers) must go in a separate, self-contained appendix, even if it is already in the record. Do not put pleadings, motions, briefs, or orders already on the docket in an appendix; cite them by docket entry. Pro se litigants not authorized to e-file are exempt. Order: cover page, table of contents (describing each item by content and its App.__ page), then each item preceded by a slip sheet. Number the first slip sheet “App. 1” and run continuously in the lower right-hand corner; cite specific App.__ pages in briefs. Every page must be text-searchable (check the OCR), with one PDF bookmark per item. Do not duplicate material already in an ap

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Multi-volume and sealed appendices
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Multi-volume and sealed appendices: Split into consecutively numbered volumes if the appendix exceeds the e-filing size limit or contains sealed material. Pagination runs continuously across volumes, no document is split between volumes, every volume’s table of contents covers the whole appendix, and each cover page states its App.__ range. When moving to seal, file a public volume and a separate sealed volume numbered “Sealed.App.1” onward and cited as “Sealed.App.__.” A sealed item’s description in the public table of contents may be generic or omitted if needed.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Joint discovery and case management plan
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Joint discovery and case management plan: The judge’s Joint Discovery and Case Management Plan form asks for jurisdiction details (for LLCs, LLPs, and partnerships, every member’s citizenship, plus an attached affidavit or declaration), removal service dates, the elements of each claim and defense with supporting authority, related cases, unserved parties, and discovery, settlement, ADR, and consent positions. Attach a proposed scheduling order on the court’s Word form, replacing its bracketed presumptive intervals with calendar dates, and explain any material deviation. The ADR and settlement items satisfy the Local Rule CV-88 report. Counsel must state they have read and will comply with the standing orders on the court’s website.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Scheduling and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Scheduling and extensions (trap): Presumptive civil schedule: motions to add parties or amend 30 days after the initial pretrial conference; burden-of-proof experts 180 days later; opposing experts 30 days after that; discovery closes 60 days later (requests must be answerable by then); mediation or settlement conference 21 days later; all motions except in limine 21 days after that. Parties may agree to extend discovery deadlines with written notice if later deadlines are unaffected, but the court can reject the extension. Non-discovery deadlines and continuances will not be extended, even on joint motion, without actual diligence and extraordinary cause. Rebuttal experts are due 30 days after the disclosure being rebutted. Attorney’s-fees experts are exempt; fees are sought by Rule 54(d)(2) motion after judgment.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Motions
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Motions: No motion other than in limine after the motion deadline without good cause. Overlength-brief motions are disfavored, and the court prefers an agreed briefing schedule over serial extension requests. If no dispositive motion is filed, the parties must jointly file a notice saying so, so trial can be set.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Mediation and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Mediation and settlement (trap): After discovery closes, parties and lead counsel must mediate or hold a face-to-face settlement meeting. Individual parties and counsel attend in person, not virtually; other parties send counsel and a representative with settlement authority in person, and each liability insurer sends a representative with authority to offer policy limits in person. A joint report signed by all counsel (date, attendees and capacities, whether meaningful progress was made, and prospects) is due within 7 days.

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Pretrial and trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Pretrial and trial (trap): The joint Final Pretrial Order must add to Local Rule CV-16(e): a narrative of each witness’s testimony, whether deposed, and a “probable,” “possible,” “expert,” or “record custodian” label; and a joint annotated jury charge in Word identifying the proponent of each disputed instruction with authority. Deposition designations only for witnesses unavailable under Rule 32(a)(4), with the basis briefed; live witnesses may not be presented by deposition. Trial briefs are optional unless requested. Motions in limine should not be filed as a matter of course, must follow a meet-and-confer and certify it, and must give factual background and law. Responses are due within 7 days; no replies without leave. At least one trial attorney per party must attend the final pretrial conference in person. A magistrate judge may pick the jury, pos

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Patent cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Patent cases (trap): All discovery except venue, jurisdictional, and claim-construction discovery is stayed until one business day after the claim construction hearing (initial disclosures still due 14 days after the initial pretrial conference, with preliminary infringement contentions and document production). Preliminary invalidity contentions follow 60 days later and must include § 101 and § 112 contentions. Contentions may be amended without leave on a certification that the amendment rests on newly identified material; adding patent claims needs leave, and leave is required after the final contention deadlines. Theories and prior art not in final contentions are barred at trial. Claim construction briefing is sequential, starting with the accused infringer: opening 20 pages, responsive 20, reply 10, sur-reply 10 (excluding caption, signature, certi

docs.t: Judge Andrew B. Davis (W.D. Tex.) — Referrals to the magistrate judge
docs.x: Judge Andrew B. Davis, W.D. Tex.. Referrals to the magistrate judge: Under a May 20, 2026 order, habeas (§§ 2241, 2254, and 2255, except death-penalty cases), prisoner conditions and § 1983 cases, and Social Security appeals go to an Austin magistrate judge for nondispositive matters and recommendations on dispositive motions. Other IFP applications are referred for the IFP ruling, any motion for counsel, and a § 1915(e) frivolousness recommendation. Under the scheduling orders, a referred magistrate judge may adjust scheduling order dates.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Hearings (trap)
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Hearings (trap): As a general practice, the court does not grant requests for hearings and rarely grants hearings on contested motions; it decides case by case. To ask for a hearing in a civil case, file a formal motion; in a criminal case, coordinate the formal motion with the courtroom deputy. Hearings are usually held in the morning or when the court’s schedule permits. Telephone conferences depend on the matter; contact the law clerk handling the case when the issue arises.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Contacting chambers: Scheduling matters go to the law clerk handling the case; law clerks may be contacted directly to prepare for trial or coordinate urgent matters. Emergencies: phone (915) 534-6744; fax (915) 534-6881. Calling only to ask a motion’s status is discouraged. Report important information or a resolved contested motion to the law clerk in civil cases and to the courtroom deputy in criminal cases. For a TRO or other expedited relief, follow the FRCP and Local Rules and notify the law clerk handling the case.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Motions and briefing
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Motions and briefing: No courtesy copies, and no copies of cases attached to briefs. Exceeding Local Rule page limits is discouraged; file a motion for leave if justified. A sur-reply requires leave of court. Letter briefs are accepted, “but discretion is the key.” Parties may extend deadlines by stipulation filed with the court where other pretrial dates are not affected.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Scheduling, continuances, and ADR (trap)
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Scheduling, continuances, and ADR (trap): The court enters a scheduling order setting trial once it receives an acceptable proposed scheduling order from the parties; changes require a motion. Notify the court as soon as a need to continue trial is known. The court will not continue trial because it has not ruled on a pending dispositive motion before final trial preparation must begin. If the parties are amenable to ADR, tell the court and it will order it. The court generally appoints the mediator but will consider a recommendation with a supporting explanation. Social Security appeals are routinely referred to a magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Civil trial
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Civil trial: No docket calls. The court usually holds a status conference before voir dire (jury) or opening statements (bench), and a jury charge conference at the end of the first day of trial. No pretrial submissions beyond the Local Rules. The judge conducts most of voir dire; each counsel gets 5 minutes to question the panel unless the court says otherwise, and must not turn voir dire into an opening statement. Address the court from the lectern. Trial hours, decorum, jury questionnaires, opening time, and deposition excerpts are covered in the law clerk’s letter sent after the scheduling order. Electronic proposed jury instructions, verdict forms, and findings and conclusions are accepted in WordPerfect 9.0. Parties collect their exhibits at the end of jury trials.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Criminal cases (trap): Scheduling is governed by the court’s Standing Discovery Order (not posted); changes require a motion. Pleas are referred to the magistrate judge. Counsel must confer on all motions before filing (unless an ex parte communication is justified) and state the result in the motion. The court prefers pretrial motion practice over the pretrial checklist; coordinate motions to suppress and evidentiary sentencing hearings with the courtroom deputy. Make a good-faith attempt to resolve discovery disputes before seeking court intervention. Communicate PSR objections to the probation officer rather than filing them. Attorney-conducted voir dire is allowed if the court finds it appropriate; opening time depends on the case. The court frowns on one attorney representing multiple defendants in one case.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Courtroom technology
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Courtroom technology: The courtroom has internet access (arrange ahead), a blackboard, an easel and paper, and video equipment (request well in advance), but no document presenter. Arrange equipment, your own equipment, overnight storage, and courtroom walk-throughs with the law clerk. Realtime rough transcripts are available only for trials, from the court reporter.

docs.t: Judge David Briones (W.D. Tex.) — Sanctions and pet peeves
docs.x: Judge David Briones, W.D. Tex.. Sanctions and pet peeves: The most common grounds for sanctions are discovery abuse and failing to appear for scheduled hearings. The court will not tolerate tardiness or unpreparedness.

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Summary judgment (trap): One Rule 56 motion per party, however labeled (including partial), without leave. Movants must strictly observe the Local Rules’ timing. Attach “Proposed Undisputed Facts” in a 2-column table: narrowly focused, sequentially numbered facts on the left and supporting evidence on the right. Facts not controverted as required are deemed admitted. The opposition attaches a “Response to Proposed Undisputed Facts” in 3 columns: the fact verbatim; undisputed or disputed (what part and why); and controverting evidence with an explanation, or a specific evidentiary objection. No legal argument in it; the court “will not wade through” documents to find disputes. Additional facts follow in the 2-column format, and the movant may reply to only those in the same 3-column format. Submit only evidence that supports or controverts a stated fa

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Removed cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Removed cases (trap): In every removed case, plaintiffs must replead by separately filing a complaint that conforms to Rules 8 and 9 within 14 calendar days after the 30-day remand-motion deadline expires, or within 14 days after an order denying remand. Defendants who answered in state court must replead with a separate answer conforming to Rules 8, 9, and 12 within 21 days after plaintiff’s complaint is filed.

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Bill of costs (trap)
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Bill of costs (trap): Before moving for costs, review the law summarized in the order, send the proposed bill to opposing counsel, and meet, confer, and try to submit an agreed bill. If a legitimate dispute remains, file a motion under Rule 54 and Local Rule CV-54 identifying the disagreements; the court will set a hearing at which lead trial counsel must appear and explain why they could not resolve it. The order notes, among other things, that private process server fees, postage, faxes, electronic legal research, travel, meals, and mediation fees generally are not recoverable, document translation is not interpreter compensation, and video and transcript versions of a deposition each require a showing of necessity.

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Immigration habeas cases
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Immigration habeas cases: Any party must notify the court as soon as possible if the petitioner is transferred, gets a custody redetermination hearing, receives a removal order, the order becomes administratively final, or the petitioner is removed or released. The petitioner bears this duty after filing; both sides share it once a show-cause order issues. If the other side disagrees with how the facts are characterized, it must tell the court within 3 days. The order is docketed in all pending and future “463 Habeas Corpus – Alien Detainee” cases assigned to the judge.

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Social Security referrals
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Social Security referrals: Social Security appeals assigned to the judge are referred to an El Paso magistrate judge for nondispositive pretrial matters and findings and recommendations on dispositive motions.

docs.t: Judge David C. Guaderrama (W.D. Tex.) — Chambers contacts
docs.x: Judge David C. Guaderrama, W.D. Tex.. Chambers contacts: The judge is a Senior U.S. District Judge in El Paso (525 Magoffin Avenue). The page lists the courtroom deputy and court reporter but no further hearing or filing procedures.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Proposed orders and letter briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Proposed orders and letter briefs (trap): Every motion and every response in opposition must be accompanied by a proposed order, completely separate from all other papers. Persons filing pro se or while in custody of a civil, state, or federal institution are exempt. Letter briefs are not accepted in cases on the judge’s docket.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Dispositive motions (trap): Under the judge’s scheduling order form, dispositive motions and responses are limited to 10 pages each, and replies to 5 pages. Responses are due 14 days after service of the motion and replies 7 days after service of the response; the court need not wait for a reply before ruling. Unless the court directs otherwise, a party may file no more than one motion for summary judgment without first obtaining leave of court for good cause.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Experts and Rule 702 objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Experts and Rule 702 objections (trap): Expert designations are filed and served by the dates set; Rule 26(a)(2)(B) materials are served but not filed. Rebuttal experts must be designated within 14 days of receipt of the opposing expert’s report. A Rule 702 reliability objection must be made by motion, stating the basis and identifying the objectionable testimony, within 14 days of receipt of the expert’s report or within 14 days of the expert’s deposition, if taken, whichever is later. Failure to comply strictly waives the objection.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Scheduling order and discovery
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Scheduling order and discovery: The proposed scheduling order form covers an ADR report under Local Rule CV-88, deadlines to amend pleadings and join parties, witness, expert, and exhibit designations, the discovery cutoff, and dispositive motions; the court fills in the pretrial conference and trial dates. Counsel may agree to continue discovery past the deadline, but the court will not intervene except in extraordinary circumstances, and no trial setting will be vacated because of information obtained in post-deadline discovery.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Settlement offers (trap)
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Settlement offers (trap): Parties asserting claims must make a written settlement offer by the date set, and opposing parties must respond in writing by the date set. Offers are private, not filed, and the court is not to be told of them. The parties must keep the written offers and responses, because the court will use them in assessing attorney’s fees and costs after trial.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Final pretrial conference: At least one attorney who will try the case for each party, and any unrepresented party, must attend. Party representatives with settlement authority and all others needed to negotiate a settlement must also attend. Consult Local Rule CV-16(e) for matters to be filed before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge James Nowlin (W.D. Tex.) — Magistrate judge referrals
docs.x: Judge James Nowlin, W.D. Tex.. Magistrate judge referrals: Habeas and Section 2255 cases (including capital cases), prisoner Section 1983 and federal conditions-of-confinement cases, and Social Security appeals go to an Austin magistrate judge for non-dispositive pretrial matters and recommendations on dispositive motions. In prisoner cases going to trial, the magistrate judge handles all pretrial proceedings until the pretrial order is filed. In other cases with an in forma pauperis application, the magistrate judge decides the application and any motion for appointment of counsel and recommends whether the case should be dismissed as frivolous, then returns the case.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Hearings and contact
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Hearings and contact: The court ordinarily does not hold hearings on civil motions; to ask for one, say so with reasons in the opening paragraph of the motion or response. No telephone conferences to resolve motions. Do not call about the status of civil motions or about substantive issues. Procedural questions not answered by the rules or standing orders may go to the law clerks at (915) 534-6740. Notify a law clerk immediately when a pending motion is resolved, and notify the court immediately when a motion is unopposed or the case settles. No chambers copies are required. For a TRO, after filing and assignment notify a law clerk or the courtroom deputy, try to give the other side notice, and send it a copy by fax or email.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Civil motion format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Civil motion format (trap): Every civil motion, opposition, and reply must contain: only the title below the caption on page 1; a statement of issues of no more than 1 page; a succinct statement of facts; argument with authority; and, if over 10 pages, a table of contents and table of authorities. The title page, tables, and statement of issues do not count toward the CV-7 page limit. Noncompliant filings will not be accepted. Longer briefs need leave (routinely granted); additional briefing beyond the reply needs leave; no letter briefs. Do not combine a motion to dismiss with an answer, or a response with a motion, in one document. Hyperlinking citations to Westlaw or Lexis is encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Pretrial deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Pretrial deadlines (trap): File the joint Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting (Appendix A form) within 45 days after any defendant appears (including by answer, removal, motion to dismiss, or transfer); missing it draws a show-cause order. Unless otherwise ordered: joinder, class certification, and amendment motions within 60 days after the earliest such appearance; pleading-based motions to dismiss within 90 days; discovery completed within 6 months of the Rule 26(f) conference; summary judgment motions within 1 month after the discovery deadline. A motion to dismiss does not stay discovery. Changes need a particularized showing of good cause, and extending one deadline does not extend later ones. Requests to modify the scheduling order must be by motion; any request to move the trial date must be made in writing before the discovery deadline.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Summary judgment: Attach “Proposed Undisputed Facts” in numbered paragraphs; facts not controverted are deemed admitted. The opposition’s “Response to Proposed Undisputed Facts” admits or denies each paragraph and lists “Disputed Issues of Material Fact” in a separate section. Each fact and denial needs a specific citation to competent affidavits or admissible evidence, filed with the statements; failing to cite can lead to denial or grant of the motion. Movants against a pro se party must serve the order’s form notice with Rule 56 and the order attached.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Discovery, extensions, and ADR
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Discovery, extensions, and ADR: Discovery matters are routinely referred to the magistrate judge. Discovery extensions may be stipulated between the parties without court approval, but extensions to answer require an agreed motion and proposed order. ADR is required in almost all civil cases; the scheduling order sets the deadline to complete it and to notify the court of the provider and date. Removing parties should attach all state-court filings and the state docket sheet.

docs.t: Judge Kathleen Cardone (W.D. Tex.) — Patent cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Kathleen Cardone, W.D. Tex.. Patent cases (trap): A separate patent standing order applies in every division and replaces the pretrial-deadlines order. Preliminary infringement contentions with document production are due within 30 days after any defendant appears; the patent RPPM is due within 45 days, listing the plaintiff’s other W.D. Tex. cases on the same patents from the last 2 years.
