docs.t: Judge Nicholas A. Danella (N.D. Ala.) — Magistrate consent and early conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas A. Danella, N.D. Ala.. Magistrate consent and early conference (trap): After the triggering filing (motion to dismiss, motion to remand, or answer), all parties must elect on magistrate judge jurisdiction within 45 days, or the Clerk reassigns the case to a randomly drawn district judge; failing to submit the form also leads to reassignment. A telephone status conference is set 21 days after the triggering filing. Forms submitted through CM/ECF go to the Clerk, not the docket; the judge learns of elections only if consent is unanimous, and declining has no adverse consequences.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas A. Danella (N.D. Ala.) — Rule 26(f) and scheduling
docs.x: Judge Nicholas A. Danella, N.D. Ala.. Rule 26(f) and scheduling: Confer within 21 days of the Rule 26 order, covering settlement or mediation, a discovery plan with an ESI protocol, and any HIPAA protective order; if the parties can’t agree on logistics, immediately file a joint notice. Exchange initial disclosures at least 7 days before the meeting. File the joint report within 14 days after the meeting, including case complexity, ADR interest, any Rule 502 clawback agreement, and whether any party anticipates seeking fees and on what basis. The Appendix A and B templates are encouraged. Sample scheduling order: depositions limited to 7 hours; supplementation no later than 14 days before the close of discovery; a Rule 502(b) and (d) non-waiver provision; telephone status conferences about every 6 months. Motions to amend must attach the complete executed amended pleading.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas A. Danella (N.D. Ala.) — Settlement conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas A. Danella, N.D. Ala.. Settlement conference (trap): Under the sample scheduling order, the parties must hold an in-person settlement conference no later than 30 days before the close of discovery. Within 5 days afterward, counsel must each email chambers separately and confidentially, stating only whether the case settled and, if not, whether the parties are amenable to mediation. Report mediation results in a joint status report within a week of completion. Notify the court of any settlement within 2 business days.

docs.t: Judge Nicholas A. Danella (N.D. Ala.) — Pretrial schedule (trap)
docs.x: Judge Nicholas A. Danella, N.D. Ala.. Pretrial schedule (trap): Trial dates are “hard” settings on a Monday, not trial-ready dates. An initial telephonic pretrial conference is held 21 days before trial and the final pretrial conference 4 days before (a Thursday); attorneys from outside the division or district may ask to appear by phone at least 2 business days ahead if one attorney per party attends in person. 35 days before trial: witness lists (with deposition page and line designations) and exhibit lists, followed by an immediate meet and confer on objections. 28 days before: motions in limine (no more than 5 without leave, no replies), optional trial briefs (10 pages maximum), and damages lists including attorneys’ fees. 14 days before: opposition briefs on motions in limine, responsive trial briefs, objections to damages, witnesses, designations, and exhibits, counter-designations

docs.t: Judge Nicholas A. Danella (N.D. Ala.) — Fee-shifting and EEOC cases
docs.x: Judge Nicholas A. Danella, N.D. Ala.. Fee-shifting and EEOC cases: A party that may seek fees (other than as a sanction) must keep contemporaneous time records to the nearest 1/10 hour, reviewed monthly, and certify compliance in any fee petition. In cases requiring an EEOC charge, plaintiff files the charges and the EEOC’s responses, including the right-to-sue notice, with the Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures.

docs.t: Judge Sharon Lovelace Blackburn (N.D. Ala.) — Guilty pleas
docs.x: Judge Sharon Lovelace Blackburn, N.D. Ala.. Guilty pleas: Judge Blackburn does not require a written Guilty Plea Advice of Rights Certification. If counsel chooses to complete one and make it part of the record, it should be e-filed before the change-of-plea hearing.

docs.t: Judge Sharon Lovelace Blackburn (N.D. Ala.) — Chambers and contact
docs.x: Judge Sharon Lovelace Blackburn, N.D. Ala.. Chambers and contact: Chambers are in the Hugo L. Black U.S. Courthouse, Birmingham. Proposed orders go to blackburn_chambers@alnd.uscourts.gov (chambers phone 205-278-1810); the civil CM/ECF helpdesk is blackburn_helpdesk@alnd.uscourts.gov (205-278-2074).

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Chambers contact
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Chambers contact: Email proposed orders to cornelius_chambers@alnd.uscourts.gov. Civil CM/ECF questions go to cornelius_helpdesk@alnd.uscourts.gov or (205) 278-1930.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Pretrial conference (trap): The pretrial conference is held in chambers at the Hugo L. Black U.S. Courthouse in Birmingham. Attorneys outside the division or district may ask to participate by telephone by notifying chambers at least 2 business days ahead, as long as one attorney for each party attends in person. The joint proposed pretrial order is emailed to chambers by the date the court sets, following the sample form: agreed summary for voir dire, numbered stipulated facts (read to the jury as true), contested fact issues, agreed propositions of law suitable for preliminary instructions, each side’s positions, and pending motions. Counsel must notify later-appearing attorneys of the conference.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Witness and exhibit lists (trap)
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Witness and exhibit lists (trap): Witness lists (including experts) and exhibit lists are due no later than 30 days before trial; unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded unless the parties agree or the court finds good cause. Listing a witness waives any objection to another party calling that witness. Objections to deposition testimony (with the relevant excerpts) and to exhibits are due within 14 days after the lists are filed; undisclosed objections are waived except under Rules 402 and 403. Make listed exhibits available for inspection and copying. Itemized damages and equitable relief, with amounts and computation method, are due 30 calendar days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Motions in limine: File motions in limine at least 14 days before trial, with supporting memoranda.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Jury submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Jury submissions (trap): At least 5 business days before trial, jointly email any special voir dire questions in Word, marking disputed questions in bold and identifying the requesting party; don’t repeat topics in the court’s voir dire template. Also at least 5 business days before trial, file a joint proposed jury charge covering elements, definitions, damages items, and calculation methods, using Eleventh Circuit or state pattern instructions with any deviation identified and supported. Number each instruction with authority, mark disputed items in bold with the requesting party, and email a Word copy. The court’s preliminary and standard instructions need not be submitted. Requested verdict forms or interrogatories are due by the trial date, filed and emailed in Word.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Exhibits at trial
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Exhibits at trial: A party offering as many as six exhibits must premark them with Clerk labels and give the courtroom deputy a PDF of every exhibit offered. By trial, serve and file the premarked exhibit list; trial won’t ordinarily pause for opposing counsel to inspect an exhibit that was made available. Attorney voir dire questions may be asked from the witness box.

docs.t: Judge Staci G. Cornelius (N.D. Ala.) — Confidential information and medical records
docs.x: Judge Staci G. Cornelius, N.D. Ala.. Confidential information and medical records: Follow the Civil Administrative Procedures Manual for personal, sealed, or protected information in trial evidence and the transcript, which is public; testimony may be stricken or redacted if private information is mentioned. The pretrial order can include a HIPAA provision authorizing counsel to inspect medical records and interview providers, and the judge posts a standard Qualified HIPAA Protective Order limiting use of health information to the case and requiring its return or destruction at the end.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Contact
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Contact: Courtroom deputy: Denise Ambrosio, 918.699.4725, Denise_Ambrosio@oknd.uscourts.gov. Chambers: 333 West Fourth St., Room 411, Tulsa (918.699.4795).

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Before trial
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Before trial: Give the court as much advance notice as possible of any particularly difficult question of law or evidence. Provide objections to proposed jury instructions, with pertinent case law, before trial. Motions in limine filed after the pretrial conference are untimely and will not be considered.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Deposition designations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Deposition designations (trap): Designations and counter-designations are exchanged and FILED as a pleading under Rule 26(a)(3) listing witness, page, line, and basis for objection (not the transcript itself). Highlighted transcripts (different colors for designations and counter-designations, objections annotated in the margins) are SUBMITTED in hard copy, not filed, to the Court Clerk no later than 10 days before trial. Objections are considered only after a personal meeting between counsel; unresolved objections are then FILED as a separate motion or objection with a table of page, line, and basis, without transcripts attached.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Voir dire and openings
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Voir dire and openings: Attorney voir dire happens only if approved before trial, and is limited to 10–15 minutes per side unless more time is approved in advance. No questions previewing evidence or law, statements disguised as questions, hypotheticals, explanations of the burden of proof, or attempts to extract promises from jurors. Openings are limited to 15–20 minutes per side unless the case is unusually complex, and may be substantially reduced per party in multiparty cases. Openings outline the evidence; no argument.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Exhibits
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Exhibits: Mark exhibits before the court session, never on court time, and tell opposing counsel in advance which exhibits you will use that day. Unobjected exhibits are offered and received without formal identification. Have the witness notebook on the stand before questioning about a group of exhibits. Passing exhibits to the jury is for truly significant exhibits only; have a copy for each juror if possible. Juror exhibit books are encouraged with prior approval.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Witnesses and examination (trap)
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Witnesses and examination (trap): Stand when addressing the court or examining, and use the lectern unless brief. Examination is limited to direct, cross, one redirect, and one recross except in exceptional circumstances. Do not greet or introduce yourself to adverse witnesses; begin cross without preliminaries. Address adult witnesses by surname. Only the attorney handling a witness may raise or respond to objections for that witness. For an unavailable witness, the same reader must read a single witness’s designated testimony throughout, absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Jury protocol
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Jury protocol: Address the jury only from the lectern and at a respectful distance. Keep objections short; do not argue objections or rulings, or make motions (such as for mistrial), in the jury’s presence. Keep bench conferences to a minimum. Do not ask the court to declare a witness an expert in front of the jury.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Courtroom conduct (trap): No beverages, including bottled water, and no gum, mints, or candy. Do not leave the courtroom during trial without leave, and do not address opposing counsel directly in open court without leave. Computers are allowed if unobtrusive and cleared with the courtroom deputy before the morning of trial. Familiarity with Local General Rule 3 (courtroom behavior) is expected.

docs.t: Judge Claire Eagan (N.D. Okla.) — Video testimony and juror notebooks
docs.x: Judge Claire Eagan, N.D. Okla.. Video testimony and juror notebooks: Videotaped testimony may be edited and presented by subject matter, combining witnesses; get objections ruled on early enough to edit the video. In complex cases, identical juror notebooks are allowed (preliminary instructions, admitted or agreed exhibits, stipulations, and agreed materials such as photographs, expert CVs, glossaries, and timelines). Counsel must confer on contents before trial. The posted civil pretrial order form lists the required sections (admitted facts, issues of fact and law, exhibits with objections, primary and secondary witnesses, settlement status, and trial-time estimate).

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Hearings and appearances
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Hearings and appearances: Civil motions: no hearing unless set. A party may file a motion to set a hearing, granted on a sufficient showing of why argument would help; the court may also set argument on its own. A hearing does not excuse incomplete briefing. Criminal motions are generally heard at the pretrial conference; file a motion for an expedited hearing if an earlier evidentiary hearing is needed. Lead counsel must attend all pretrial conferences, civil and criminal, unless excused. Courtroom 3, Boulder Courthouse, 224 S. Boulder Ave., Tulsa; deputy Karen Perkins, 918.699.4708, Karen_Perkins@oknd.uscourts.gov.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine and Daubert
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine and Daubert: File per the scheduling order; they are typically addressed at the pretrial conference. Untimely motions in limine are not considered absent manifest injustice. Do not move to require compliance with the Federal Rules of Evidence or to exclude broad categories; target specific evidence.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Criminal continuances (trap): No proposed order needed. A motion to continue the trial setting will not be ruled on without a correct, executed speedy trial waiver on the court’s CR-06 form, from each defendant in a multi-defendant case. The waiver must name the specific excludable dates (from the current trial docket to the requested one), ideally filed with the motion. If not filed before the pretrial conference, the motion is taken up there, but the court discourages using the conference just to obtain waivers.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Criminal motions (trap): Responses are due within 7 days of the motion (LCrR 47-2). No replies without leave; if allowed, 5 pages maximum. Motions on probation or supervised release issues must state the U.S. Probation Office’s position.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Changes of plea
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Changes of plea: Email the courtroom deputy when a defendant is ready to plead. Most plea hearings are referred to the change-of-plea duty magistrate judge; instructions for plea documents follow by email. Absent good cause, file any superseding information at least 3 days before the plea hearing.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial order (trap): The judge’s form requires a single joint statement of the case identifying every cause of action, affirmative defense, counterclaim, and cross-claim (no separate statements), plus an itemization of damages and other relief. Exhibit lists: joint and per-party, two columns (exhibit in offer sequence, no subheadings; objection with the governing Federal Rule). Exclude impeachment or rebuttal items, expert CVs and reports, depositions, demonstratives, and pleadings. Furnish all exhibits before the pretrial conference; late exhibits need notice, an immediate written application, and manifest injustice. Witnesses are listed as primary and secondary with the subjects of testimony; testimony on other subjects and unlisted witnesses are not allowed absent court order.

docs.t: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell (N.D. Okla.) — Trial exhibits and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Gregory Kent Frizzell, N.D. Okla.. Trial exhibits and courtroom: Prepare separate exhibit notebooks for the witness stand, opposing counsel, the court, and the law clerk. Use of the electronic evidence presentation system is encouraged; inexperienced users should schedule training with the deputy. Do not address opposing counsel directly in open court. No food or beverages during trial (water is provided); at non-trial matters, water only, in a lidded container.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Lead Trial Counsel (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Lead Trial Counsel (trap): Each party must designate one Lead Trial Counsel in its first submission (including reassigned cases); the designation can’t change without prior approval. Lead Trial Counsel must personally attend all conferences and be involved in discovery disputes.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Initial conference and scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Initial conference and scheduling (trap): The court sets an initial conference promptly, even before issues are joined. At least 3 business days before, email chambers a report of agreements and disagreements plus a proposed plan on the court’s Case Management Plan form; redline any change beyond filling blanks. This departs from Rule 26(f) and LCvR 16-1(b). Most cases must be trial-ready within 9 months or less of the Case Management Order. Interim discovery deadlines may be extended by consent, but the discovery completion date only for extraordinary circumstances, never by consent. Form limits: interrogatories only as LCvR 33-1 allows; no document requests or requests to admit later than 30 days before discovery closes; depositions limited to one business day each and proceed concurrently. Rebuttal or other experts beyond disclosures need leave so

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Filings and courtesy copies (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Filings and courtesy copies (trap): Courtesy copy required for any filing with more than five exhibits or over 100 pages including exhibits: an exact copy of the filed version with ECF header, exhibits tabbed in numerical order, sealed pages watermarked. Summary judgment and limine papers also need hard courtesy copies delivered to chambers on the filing date. Every amended or corrected filing, and every motion to amend, must include a redline; if amendment needs no motion, email the redline to CM-ECFIntake_OKND@oknd.uscourts.gov, copying opposing counsel.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Discovery disputes and depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Discovery disputes and depositions (trap): Before raising a dispute, confer in person, by video, or by phone, including at least one Lead Trial Counsel conference. The other side must make itself available within 2 business days. If unresolved in 10 business days (or at impasse), the party seeking discovery may move, stating the Lead Trial Counsel conference occurred. Late-raised issues are unlikely to get relief. Privilege logs must be detailed (including attorneys involved), produced and updated on a rolling basis, and certified by counsel after review. The court may order in camera review. Form objections are limited to “objection, form”; no coaching. Disputes during a deposition may be raised by joint call to chambers or the magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Civil pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Civil pretrial (trap): Rule 26(a)(3) disclosures may be made 21 (not 30) days before trial. A joint proposed Pretrial Order (14 listed items, including particularized claims, damages amounts, a final binding witness list in order of appearance, and exhibit lists with objections) is due 1 week before trial, with a hard courtesy copy. Summary judgment and limine briefing must finish within 6 weeks of discovery close; oral argument is at the final pretrial conference, where a firm trial date is set. One limine brief per party absent leave, with courtesy copies of referenced exhibits; limine motions are usually decided the morning of trial. Jury charges due 1 week before trial (later ones are not considered absent unforeseeable issues); proposed preliminary instructions and voir dire requests 3 business days before. The court conducts voir dire and uses

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Trial exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Trial exhibits (trap): Provide the court copies of exhibits 3 business days before trial, and hand the bench a copy of each exhibit (two in criminal trials) when giving the original to a witness. Number both sides’ exhibits. Exhibits not admitted and presented, discussed, or argued at trial are removed from jury binders even if preadmitted, and are not considered on dispositive motions. Deposition designations: file under Rule 26(a)(3) and LCvR 30-1; submit color-highlighted, annotated transcripts in hard copy and file unresolved objections (after a personal meeting) no later than 7 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Trial conduct: Civil openings 15–20 minutes per side; in criminal cases “take as much time as you dare.” Plaintiff sums up first; rebuttal summation only where there are two or more defense summations, or in unusual circumstances. No beverages, including bottled water. Stand and use the lectern; one redirect and one recross; no greeting adverse witnesses; no motions or argument on objections before the jury. Computers must be cleared with the deputy before the morning of trial. Junior attorneys are encouraged to participate, and requests for argument may be granted to give them experience.

docs.t: Judge John David Russell (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge John David Russell, N.D. Okla.. Criminal cases (trap): Witness and exhibit lists are due to the Clerk for chambers 3 business days before trial, which differs from LCrR 23. Limine motions must be served 2 weeks before trial and oppositions filed 1 week before, with courtesy copies. Brady material known at indictment is due within 2 weeks of indictment, even during plea talks; later Brady material within 2 weeks of discovery and at least 4 weeks before trial or plea. Giglio material is due 4 weeks before trial or plea, and immediately if developed later. Protective orders are entered only on the judge’s posted form; contact the courtroom deputy (Christy Butler, 918-699-4707) for a formatted copy.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Motions: conferral and form (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Motions: conferral and form (trap): Every motion must state on page one whether it is opposed or unopposed. An opposed motion needs a statement of conferral describing how conferral took place and, if concurrence was refused, why. Motions lacking either may be summarily denied. Motions for judicial notice or to declare an uncontested issue are disfavored: file a stipulation instead. Unopposed motions may be stricken absent good cause for a ruling. Cite unpublished cases by Westlaw citation; if none exists, attach the case.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine (trap): One omnibus motion in limine per party, capped at 40 pages. File by the scheduling-order deadline; untimely motions are not considered absent manifest injustice. Target specific evidence, not compliance with the Rules of Evidence. Raise objections to scientific and expert testimony by timely motion in limine, and Daubert issues by Daubert motion under the scheduling order.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Civil extensions and settlement
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Civil extensions and settlement: Extension requests must be in writing, filed at least 48 hours before the deadline absent emergency, and meet LCvR 7-1 and Tenth Circuit standards. Extensions will likely affect the trial setting; the gap between discovery cutoff and trial is not a cushion. Parties are expected to attend a settlement conference midway through discovery; continuances because discovery is incomplete need good cause.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Hearings, pretrial, and civil trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Hearings, pretrial, and civil trial (trap): For evidentiary hearings, email witness and exhibit lists to the courtroom deputy 3 business days before and bring 4 paper copies. Counsel must meet before the pretrial conference to review all exhibits, and be ready to argue exhibit objections, pending dispositive motions, and motions in limine; the court aims to end the conference with the case trial-ready. One week before the conference, provide the court 2 notebooks of exhibits with remaining objections. Civil trials trail criminal cases on the docket; a continuance will not be granted because of the number of criminal cases, and counsel must be ready if they all resolve.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal hearings and status reports
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Criminal hearings and status reports: All counsel, including out-of-state counsel, must attend criminal hearings in person; arrive 15 minutes early. Notify the deputy early if a pretrial will exceed 10 minutes or a sentencing or revocation 30 minutes. File the discovery joint status report as “Notice (Other)” with a substantive update (outstanding materials, reasons, timing, anticipated discovery motions). Not filing it without notice is unacceptable, including when a plea is merely anticipated; if ready to plead, notify the deputy by the JSR due date.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal continuances and motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Criminal continuances and motions (trap): Title every motion unopposed, agreed, or opposed, with each party’s (including co-defendants’) position. No proposed order needed. Unless the case is declared complex, a trial continuance requires a correct CR-06 speedy trial waiver from each defendant, signed by defendant and counsel, naming the specific excludable dates; the court will not rule without it. Responses within 7 days (LCrR 47-2); no replies without leave, then 5 pages. One motion to suppress per defendant absent leave. Supervised-release motions must state Probation’s position. Posted criminal trial dates: Nov. 16 and Dec. 14, 2026; Jan. 25, Feb. 15, Mar. 15, Apr. 19, May 17, June 21, and July 19, 2027.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Changes of plea
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Changes of plea: Email the courtroom deputy with good and bad dates; most plea hearings go to the criminal duty magistrate judge. Plea petition and agreement are generally due 3 business days before the hearing, and any superseding information 3 days before, absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Courtroom protocol (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Courtroom protocol (trap): All electronic devices must be off; use at trial requires approval on good cause. Only bottled water; no food, gum, or mints. Only the examining attorney raises objections or argues at sidebar for that witness. No greeting adverse witnesses. Handle physical evidence with gloves, and give the deputy advance notice of biohazard exhibits by the exhibit-list deadline. Junior attorneys are strongly encouraged to participate, and multiple attorneys may speak to create opportunities for them.

docs.t: Judge John Frederick Heil III (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order form
docs.x: Judge John Frederick Heil III, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial order form: The judge’s form requires itemized dollar damages per element, separately listed affirmative defenses, specific exhibit identification (records by provider and dates, manual sections by page, videos by date and subject), and no separate statements of the case or issues of law. Stipulations are given separately at the pretrial conference and read to the jury; unlisted witnesses may not testify.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Proposed orders (trap): All proposed orders must follow the template posted on the judge’s page: caption with a center vertical border line (not parentheses), 0.25-inch first-line indents, left-justified, 13 pt. double-spaced Century Schoolbook text, block quotes for 50 or more words, and record cites as [ECF No. ## at ##]. Signature block reads “Sara E. Hill,” not all caps. The template adds: no page number on page 1, page numbers and footnotes in 12 pt. Century Schoolbook, one space between sentences. Noncompliant orders may have to be corrected, delaying entry.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Courtesy copies and briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Courtesy copies and briefs (trap): Any filing over 50 pages including exhibits needs a physical courtesy copy, an exact duplicate of the filed version, with numbered exhibit tabs and sealed pages clearly marked. No table of authorities is required, despite LCvR 7-1(d) and LCrR 47-5(b); the rest of those rules still applies.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Civil motions, extensions, and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Civil motions, extensions, and sealing (trap): Before any motion (except ex parte or emergency), make a meaningful effort to confer with all parties; every motion must certify conferral or explain why it could not occur. Extension requests are due at least 2 full business days before the deadline absent emergency or good cause; no proposed order needed. Scheduling-order extensions may affect the trial setting, and repeated requests may prompt a status conference. Strict adherence to LCvR 5.2; motions to seal must be filed at least 2 full business days before the filing deadline.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine: Combine all motions in limine in one filing, and attach any challenged trial exhibit. Do not seek orders to follow the Rules of Evidence or to exclude broad categories.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Exhibits and technology (trap)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Exhibits and technology (trap): For trials and evidentiary hearings, provide separate exhibit notebooks for the witness stand, opposing counsel, the court, and the law clerk, at least 2 full business days before. Electronic exhibits need placeholder pages in the notebooks and electronic copies for opposing counsel and the court. Test courtroom technology with the deputy in advance; little time will be allowed for technical problems, especially in jury trials.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Trial and courtroom
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Trial and courtroom: Examinations, openings, and closings from the lectern. Keep objections concise; no arguing objections, motions, expert designations, or discovery disputes before the jury. Trials may trail; criminal trials go before civil, and counsel must be ready to start as soon as the preceding case ends. Water is provided at counsel table; no other food or drink in front of the bar without approval. Electronic devices allowed for those with business before the court if silent and not distracting.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Criminal continuances and motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Criminal continuances and motions (trap): Extension requests are due 2 full business days before the deadline; no proposed order. Motions affecting the trial setting are held until every defendant files a correct CR-06 speedy trial waiver, signed by defendant and counsel and naming the specific excludable dates. Every motion must state on page one whether it is opposed and each party’s position, including co-defendants, or may be summarily denied. Responses within 7 days; no replies without leave, then 5 pages. Supervised-release motions must state Probation’s position. Motions are generally heard at the pretrial conference; for evidentiary hearings, email witness and exhibit lists to the deputy and deliver 4 paper copies at least 2 full business days before.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Pleas, trial prep, and sentencing (criminal)
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Pleas, trial prep, and sentencing (criminal): Email the deputy (Lauren Lewis, Lauren_Lewis@oknd.uscourts.gov) with good dates and dates to avoid. Plea petition and agreement are due 3 full business days before the hearing (CR-05 form encouraged); superseding charges 3 business days before, absent good cause. Email objections to jury instructions and case law to SEHIntake_OKND@oknd.uscourts.gov. Submit sentencing letters and materials at least 1 week before sentencing.

docs.t: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill (N.D. Okla.) — Junior lawyers and communications
docs.x: Judge Sara Elizabeth Hill, N.D. Okla.. Junior lawyers and communications: The court may grant oral argument it would not usually set, and allow multiple attorneys to speak, to give new lawyers experience. Scheduling and administrative questions go to the courtroom deputy.

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial order listings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial order listings (trap): An exhibit or witness not listed in the proposed Pretrial Order is excluded at trial unless allowed on written motion for good cause. Incorporating the other side’s exhibits or witnesses by reference is not permitted. Number or Bates-stamp multipage exhibits and state the page count; list photographs by number with descriptions rather than as a category; use Rule 1006 summaries for categories such as medical bills. Counsel are expected to follow Local Rule 16.1. The posted pretrial order form lists the required sections (admitted facts, issues of fact and law, exhibits with objections, primary and secondary witnesses, settlement status, trial-time estimate).

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Pretrial conference: Be ready to argue exhibit objections, pending dispositive motions, and pending motions in limine; the court aims to end the conference with the case ready for trial. Also raise anything likely to cause sidebars or long argument at trial. Counsel must meet before the conference to review all proposed exhibits; claims at trial of never having seen a listed exhibit are disfavored.

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Motions in limine and Daubert
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Motions in limine and Daubert: Strongly encouraged for complicated evidentiary issues; file by the scheduling-order deadline for decision at the pretrial conference. Untimely motions are not considered absent manifest injustice. Raise objections to scientific and expert testimony by timely motion in limine, and Daubert issues by Daubert motion under the scheduling order.

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Daily copy (trap)
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Daily copy (trap): Daily transcripts are not allowed without prior approval, only in exceptional circumstances, on a motion heard at the pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Voir dire
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Voir dire: Attorney voir dire is allowed with time limits, 10–15 minutes per side unless more is approved before trial. Be ready to discuss voir dire areas and requested court questions at the pretrial conference. No previewing evidence or law, statements disguised as questions, hypotheticals, burden-of-proof explanations, or seeking promises from jurors.

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Exhibit and juror notebooks
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Exhibit and juror notebooks: Prepare separate exhibit notebooks for the witness stand, opposing counsel, the court, and the law clerk; in voluminous cases, tailor notebooks to each witness or witness group. Try to agree on a joint exhibit set, with objected exhibits in separate plaintiff’s or defendant’s sets. Juror notebooks are rarely used; raise them at the pretrial conference and confer on contents before trial. Learn the Video Evidence Presentation System before trial (training through the Clerk’s office).

docs.t: Judge Terence C. Kern (N.D. Okla.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Terence C. Kern, N.D. Okla.. Trial: Juror note-taking is permitted; in 1–3 day trials the court gives no note-taking instruction unless asked. Closing argument follows the final instructions unless the court says otherwise.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Motions in limine (trap): Motions in limine and motions for pretrial Rule 104 evidentiary hearings are due no later than 28 days before trial; oppositions 14 days after the motion is filed. Replies are ordinarily not required but may be filed within 3 days after the opposition. Notify chambers immediately of any pretrial motion requiring an evidentiary hearing. Motions in limine on deposition objections follow a separate 7-day deadline (see deposition designations). Objections to designated interrogatory answers and requests for admission are also raised by motion in limine on the 28-day schedule; the responses themselves must be designated by number in the pretrial conference order.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Deposition designations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Deposition designations (trap): Plaintiff designates by 28 days before trial; defendant counter-designates, designates its own, and objects by 21 days; plaintiff counter-designates and objects by 14 days. By 7 days before trial, file a color copy of the excerpts (plaintiff’s designations highlighted yellow, defendant’s green, objections in the margin), plus a motion in limine indexing every unresolved objection by page and line (NECivR 30.1(f)) and certifying the meet-and-confer required by NECivR 30.1(e). Form and foundation objections not made at the deposition are waived, and unnecessary objections should be withdrawn. After the rulings, the proponent edits the video (NECivR 32.1) or transcript designations and gives the other side time to review them. Deposition testimony of nonparty witnesses who testify live (in bench trials, any live witness) i

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Exhibits, witnesses, and experts (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Exhibits, witnesses, and experts (trap): Deliver two copies of trial exhibits to chambers 14 days before trial, in binders and in electronic format. NECivR 39.3 applies except as modified. At the pretrial conference with the magistrate judge (or as that judge orders), each party emails a Word exhibit list to both the magistrate judge’s and Judge Buescher’s chambers. Witness lists go in the pretrial conference order with addresses by city and state only; full names and complete addresses must be disclosed to the other parties by the pretrial conference. A witness who does not appear when scheduled is considered withdrawn. Deliver expert disclosures to chambers, in binders or digitally, 14 days before trial; any expert whose Rule 26 disclosure is not received by then (or earlier if requested) is considered withdrawn.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Jury instructions: Meet and confer by 28 days before trial; by 21 days, file and email Word versions to chambers of a joint set of agreed instructions, a joint proposed verdict form, and, if needed, each party’s instructions on disputed issues. Instructions must be jury-ready and tailored to the case, based where possible on the Eighth Circuit Model Civil or Nebraska Civil Jury Instructions, with citations to authority. NECivR 51.1 applies except as modified. The court reads preliminary instructions after voir dire and before openings, gives the parties a preliminary set at the start of trial, holds one or more instruction conferences during trial, and gives final instructions before closing arguments.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Trial briefs and interpreters
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Trial briefs and interpreters: Trial briefs are due no later than 7 days before trial and must comply with NECivR 39.2. A party needing an interpreter must retain one (a certified court interpreter if certification exists for the language, unless the court permits otherwise) and notify the courtroom deputy, Tracy McKibben (tracy_mckibben@ned.uscourts.gov, 402-661-7351), no later than 7 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Trial schedule and jury
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Trial schedule and jury: Final pretrial conference in Courtroom 5 at 8:30 a.m. on the first day of trial; in jury cases, jury selection starts at 9 a.m. Trial hours are usually 9 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4:30 p.m., with 15-minute morning and afternoon breaks. Eight jurors are seated, and trial proceeds as long as at least six remain (NECivR 48.1). After a limited examination by the court, counsel generally get 20 minutes per party for voir dire. Jurors may take notes but may not ask or submit questions.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Courtroom practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Courtroom practice (trap): Openings: up to 30 minutes per party. Closings: 30 minutes per party; plaintiff may reserve up to 15 minutes for true rebuttal that raises nothing new. The courtroom deputy keeps time and gives a 5-minute warning on request. No speaking objections; a foundation objection must state what foundation is lacking. Keep bench conferences to a minimum. Recross is not normally permitted, and cross and redirect are limited to the scope of the prior examination. Unless good cause exists, counsel must use the courtroom multimedia system and their own laptops to display exhibits; arrange training with the courtroom deputy beforehand. Exhibits may not be published to the jury without the court’s consent. Question from the podium, address witnesses and parties by surname, and use the table microphones; courtroom audio, including during br

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — After submission
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. After submission: Counsel must be available to return on short notice until the verdict and keep the courtroom deputy told where they can be reached. Jury questions are normally taken up on the record with counsel and the parties present.

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Settlement (trap): Counsel for all parties must notify the court immediately of a settlement, by email or phone to the assigned magistrate judge’s chambers or to Tracy McKibben during business hours. If settlement occurs within five days before trial, contact Tracy McKibben immediately by email or phone (402-661-7351).

docs.t: Judge Brian Craig Buescher (D. Neb.) — Bench trials and contact
docs.x: Judge Brian Craig Buescher, D. Neb.. Bench trials and contact: The non-jury order repeats the motion in limine, deposition, exhibit, witness, expert, trial brief, interpreter, opening, closing (including the 15-minute rebuttal), no-recross, and settlement rules, without the jury provisions. Email proposed orders to buescher@ned.uscourts.gov. The judge sits in Omaha, Courtroom 5.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Summary judgment: Judge Gerrard resolves summary judgment motions by the earlier of 60 days after the motion is ripe or 5 days before the pretrial conference. The court’s page states that all judges enforce NECivR 7.1 and 56.1; noncompliance will at least be noted in a written order, and harsher sanctions are possible.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Sentencing schedule (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Sentencing schedule (trap): The sentencing order sets dated deadlines for: versions of the offense to probation; financial information, restitution proposals, and evaluations; the initial PSR; written objections to probation; the revised PSR and addendum; then departure and variance motions, alternative-confinement proposals, and each party’s statement of position on unresolved objections. Before defense counsel submits PSR objections, the defendant must have read the initial PSR (or had it read by an interpreter) and had a chance to voice objections. Objections first raised in a statement of position are addressed at the judge’s discretion, and no sentencing factor first raised after the statement is filed will be considered.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Sentencing evidence and briefs
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Sentencing evidence and briefs: Evidence on a motion or objection comes by affidavit, letter, report, or other document attached to the statement of position, or by oral testimony requested in the statement, which must give the nature of the testimony, why documents won’t do, each witness, and the time needed for direct. The adverse party may make a responsive request within five working days. Brief any objection raising a substantial legal issue. Departure motions need a brief grounded in guideline departure theory; Booker variance motions need a brief explaining the different principle of law that justifies a non-guideline sentence.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Tentative findings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Tentative findings (trap): The judge issues rulings and tentative findings and says whether oral testimony will be permitted. An oral objection at sentencing suffices only if no evidence and no new substantial legal issue will be offered. Otherwise, file a written objection no later than five business days before sentencing (if time does not permit, as soon as possible but no later than one business day before). If offering evidence, say why a hearing is needed, what evidence, and how long; brief any new substantial legal issue.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Criminal jury trial basics
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Criminal jury trial basics: Trial hours: 8:45 a.m. to noon and 1:15 to 4:30 p.m., with 15-minute morning and afternoon breaks. The court conducts a general voir dire, then each lawyer gets 20 minutes. Openings: 20 minutes per party. Closings: 30 minutes per party, with up to 10 minutes reserved for true rebuttal. Counsel may remain seated to question witnesses, should remain seated when digital audio is in use, and may not move about the courtroom during openings and closings when it is in use.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Jury instructions (trap): Submit requested instructions as the order setting trial directs, but no later than 1 business day before trial. Preliminary instructions are given after voir dire and before openings, with the proposed set provided to counsel before trial. Final instructions are given before closing arguments, with a “housekeeping” instruction after. An informal, off-the-record conference near the end of trial is followed by a formal on-the-record conference.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Jurors (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Jurors (trap): Be prepared to state whether you want alternates seated; if none is seated, be prepared to stipulate that 11 jurors may return a verdict whenever the 12th is excused. Jurors may take notes but may not ask questions.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Exhibits, objections, and examination
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Exhibits, objections, and examination: Pre-mark exhibits and list them on court-approved forms where practical; give received exhibits to the courtroom deputy, and turn in unoffered or unreceived listed exhibits at the close of trial. Before exhibits go to the jury, counsel confer in the deputy’s presence about which ones go. Provide the judge a copy of each exhibit. No speaking objections; a foundation objection must state what is lacking. Bench conferences should be infrequent and only for good cause. Recross is not normally permitted, and cross and redirect are limited to the scope of the prior examination.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Recording and courtroom
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Recording and courtroom: The judge uses either a court reporter or digital audio (counsel are told in advance); digital recordings are uploaded to CM/ECF after each day. Always speak into a microphone, including the presenter microphone when using the video presenter, or you will be interrupted. Courtroom audio, including during recesses, is broadcast to chambers. In Lincoln, for security, the defendant and defense counsel must use the table by the east wall, not the one by the jury box. Counsel must stay in the courthouse or be available on short notice until the verdict; jury questions are taken up on the record with the defendant present.

docs.t: Judge John Melvin Gerrard (D. Neb.) — Recusals and contact
docs.x: Judge John Melvin Gerrard, D. Neb.. Recusals and contact: The posted recusal list (last updated July 21, 2020) shows the City of Lincoln. Email proposed orders to gerrard@ned.uscourts.gov. The judge sits in Lincoln, Courtroom 3.

docs.x: Judge Joseph F. Bataillon, D. Neb.. docs.x: Judge Joseph F. Bataillon, D. Neb.. Sentencing hearing length (trap): One week before sentencing, counsel must notify the judge if the hearing is expected to last longer than one-half hour.

docs.x: Judge Joseph F. Bataillon, D. Neb.. Sentencing evidence and briefs: Evidence on a motion or objection comes by affidavit, letter, report, or other document attached to the statement of position, or by oral testimony requested in the statement, which must give the nature of the testimony, why documents won’t do, each witness, and the time needed for direct. docs.t: Judge Joseph F. Bataillon (D. Neb.) — Contact
docs.x: Judge Joseph F. Bataillon, D. Neb.. Contact: Email proposed orders to bataillon@ned.uscourts.gov. The judge sits in Omaha, Courtroom 3.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Civil jury instructions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Civil jury instructions (trap): Counsel must meet and confer, without the court, to build a complete joint set. At least two weeks before trial, file and email Word versions to chambers of a joint set of agreed instructions, a joint proposed verdict form, and, if necessary, each party’s instructions on disputed issues (see also the Final Progression Order and NECivR 51.1). Instructions must be jury-ready and tailored to the facts, not abstract propositions of law, based where possible on the Eighth Circuit Model Civil, Nebraska Civil, or other pattern instructions. The court holds an informal, off-the-record instruction conference in chambers during trial, then a formal on-the-record conference. Final substantive instructions are given after closing arguments (civil and criminal).

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Preliminary instructions
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Preliminary instructions: In jury trials the court reads a standard preliminary Instruction No. 1 after voir dire and before openings; counsel receive a copy 10 days before trial. In criminal cases, final instructions follow the Trial Order.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Trial hours and jury
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Trial hours and jury: Jury trials usually run 9 a.m. to noon and 1:30 to 4:30 p.m.; bench trials 9 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4:30 p.m., with 15-minute morning and afternoon breaks. Civil juries generally have eight jurors and no alternates (NECivR 48.1). Criminal trials seat 12 jurors and usually one alternate. After a limited examination by the court (NECivR 47.1(a) in civil cases), counsel generally get 20 minutes per party for voir dire. Jurors may take notes but may not ask or submit questions.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Openings and closings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Openings and closings (trap): Openings: up to 30 minutes. Closings: 30 minutes per party. In jury trials, the plaintiff or government may reserve up to 10 minutes (one-third of its time) for rebuttal, never more than half the time actually used; in bench trials, closings are on request and the plaintiff may reserve up to 15 minutes. Rebuttal must be true rebuttal and raise nothing not addressed in the first argument (in criminal cases, or in the defendant’s closing). The courtroom deputy keeps time and gives a 5-minute warning on request.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Objections and examination (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Objections and examination (trap): No speaking objections in jury trials; a foundation objection must state what foundation is lacking. Ask for a bench conference and allow the court reporter time to set up; keep them to a minimum. Recross is not permitted (in bench trials, not normally). Cross is limited to the scope of direct, and redirect to the scope of cross. Question from the podium unless directed otherwise, and refer to witnesses and parties by surname absent permission.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Exhibits and evidence presentation (trap)
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Unless good cause exists, counsel must use the courtroom multimedia system, including the video presenter, and their own laptops to display exhibits; contact the courtroom deputy for training and test audio, video, and electronic presentations before trial. The deputy generally controls publishing to the jury on the judge’s instruction.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Courtroom logistics
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. Courtroom logistics: Plaintiff’s or the government’s counsel uses the tables nearest the jury box; defense counsel the tables farthest away. Pull the podium and table microphones about six inches in front of you; mute them for client conferences. Anything said in the courtroom, including during breaks, is broadcast to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — After submission
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. After submission: Counsel must be available to return on short notice until the verdict and keep the courtroom deputy told where they can be reached. Jury questions are normally taken up on the record with counsel present.

docs.t: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr. (D. Neb.) — Cross-references and contact
docs.x: Judge Robert F. Rossiter Jr., D. Neb.. docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Motions and briefing
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Motions and briefing: Leave to exceed the prescribed page length must be sought by motion. Label exhibits clearly. If memoranda reference deposition excerpts, the judge prefers having the full condensed transcript available. Hearings on civil motions are rare; put all arguments and authority in the memoranda supporting and opposing the motion.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Proposed orders (trap): File a proposed order as an attachment to every non-dispositive motion. Submit proposed orders, proposed jury instructions, and proposed findings and conclusions in PDF through CM/ECF.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Emergency motions
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Emergency motions: For TROs and select discovery motions, do not call chambers until the matter is assigned to Judge Dever; then tell the intake deputy clerk it needs immediate attention. Except in admiralty matters, the judge generally asks the movant to confer with opposing counsel to try to agree on temporary injunctive action pending the preliminary injunction hearing.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Protective orders and sealing (trap): Before submitting a proposed consent protective order, review Hall v. United Airlines, Inc., 296 F. Supp. 2d 652, 678–80 (E.D.N.C. 2003), and Local Civil Rule 79.2. The judge’s model language: before filing material designated confidential, confer with the producing party; if it wants sealing, file under L. Civ. R. 79.2 with notice to it, and within 10 days of that notice the producing party (not the filer) must move to seal with a supporting memorandum. If no timely motion is filed, the materials are deemed unsealed without further order.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Civil pretrial
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Civil pretrial: Pretrial is set after all dispositive motions are heard, and the pretrial conference usually comes about two weeks before trial; it will not automatically be continued if dispositive motions are still pending. Submit all expert material (CVs, reports, depositions, and objections to qualifications) to chambers before trial for the court’s gatekeeping function. The judge prefers a hearing near trial to rule on Pretrial Order objections; at trial, all exhibits are deemed admitted except those on which ruling was reserved. Parties may consent to a magistrate judge, including trial on a date certain.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Criminal terms (trap)
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Criminal terms (trap): Motions to continue (including by Probation) are due at least 5 business days before the session begins, absent exigent circumstances, with a proposed order; orders continuing arraignment must contain speedy-trial language from 18 U.S.C. § 3161(h). All attorneys, agents, and defendants must be seated at 9:00 a.m. on the first day of the term, when the docket is called; defendants to be arraigned must hear the half-hour “litany,” and a late defendant will be taken into custody. Arraignments and Rule 11 pleas are on day one, with sentencings and motions following. All juries for the term are picked the same day; express trial-order preferences to the courtroom deputy at least a week before the term.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Scheduling conflicts
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Scheduling conflicts: Send “conflict letters” to each judge whose docket is affected; staff will resolve the conflict. Federal prosecutors and defenders should try to hand off routine matters internally first.

docs.t: Judge James C. Dever III (E.D.N.C.) — Courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge James C. Dever III, E.D.N.C.. Courtroom conduct: Cell phones are prohibited in the courtroom. The judge is punctual and expects the same; gamesmanship, sandbagging, name-calling, or other unbecoming conduct will not be tolerated.
